entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.linearMomentum
entries.docstring:
The linear momentum of the free particle along a trajectory.

This is given by the classical one-dimensional expression `p = m v`,
where `m` is the particle mass and `v` is the velocity.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable
def linearMomentum (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.linearMomentum_conserved_of_velocity_const
entries.docstring: If a free-particle trajectory has constant velocity, then its linear momentum is constant.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearMomentum_conserved_of_velocity_const (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory)
    (h : ∃ v₀, ∀ t, s.velocity q t = v₀) :
    ∃ p, ∀ t, s.linearMomentum q t = p

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.linearMomentum_conserved
entries.docstring:
A free particle satisfying the equation of motion conserves linear momentum.

Newton's second law implies that the acceleration vanishes, so the velocity is constant.
Since the particle mass is fixed, the linear momentum is constant in time.
entries.snippet:
theorem linearMomentum_conserved (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory)
    (h : ∀ t, s.NewtonsSecondLaw q t) (hcont : ContDiff ℝ 2 q) :
    ∃ p, ∀ t, s.linearMomentum q t = p

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions.toInitialConditions
entries.docstring:
Convert two-position initial conditions to standard initial conditions at `t = 0`.

  Obtained by solving the 2×2 linear system from the trajectory formula at `t₁` and `t₂`.
  See `toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₁` and `toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₂` in
  section D.2 for the correctness proofs (valid under `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`).
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def toInitialConditions (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions) : InitialConditions where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities.toInitialConditions
entries.docstring:
Convert two-velocity initial conditions to standard initial conditions at `t = 0`.

  Obtained by solving the 2×2 linear system from the velocity formula at `t₁` and `t₂`.
  See `toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₁` and `toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₂` in
  section D.3 for the correctness proofs (valid under `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`).
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def toInitialConditions (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities) : InitialConditions where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions.toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₁
entries.docstring:
The trajectory from `toInitialConditions` passes through `x_t₁` at time `t₁`,
  provided `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₁ (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions)
    (hΔ : sin (S.ω * (IC.t₂ - IC.t₁)) ≠ 0) :
    (IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S IC.t₁ = IC.x_t₁

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions.toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₂
entries.docstring:
The trajectory from `toInitialConditions` passes through `x_t₂` at time `t₂`,
  provided `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_trajectory_at_t₂ (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoPositions)
    (hΔ : sin (S.ω * (IC.t₂ - IC.t₁)) ≠ 0) :
    (IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S IC.t₂ = IC.x_t₂

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities.toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₁
entries.docstring:
The trajectory from `toInitialConditions` has velocity `v_t₁` at time `t₁`,
  provided `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₁ (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities)
    (hΔ : sin (S.ω * (IC.t₂ - IC.t₁)) ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ ((IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S) IC.t₁ = IC.v_t₁

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities.toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₂
entries.docstring:
The trajectory from `toInitialConditions` has velocity `v_t₂` at time `t₂`,
  provided `sin (S.ω * (t₂ - t₁)) ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_velocity_at_t₂ (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditionsFromTwoVelocities)
    (hΔ : sin (S.ω * (IC.t₂ - IC.t₁)) ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ ((IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S) IC.t₂ = IC.v_t₂

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.AmplitudePhase.toInitialConditions
entries.docstring:
Convert amplitude–phase initial conditions to standard initial conditions at `t = 0`, via
  `x₀ = A cos φ` and `v₀ = A ω sin φ`.

  See `toInitialConditions_trajectory_eq_cos` and `toInitialConditions_velocity_eq_sin` in
  section E.3 for the correctness proofs.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def toInitialConditions (S : HarmonicOscillator) (IC : AmplitudePhase) :
    InitialConditions where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.AmplitudePhase.toInitialConditions_trajectory_eq_cos
entries.docstring:
The trajectory of amplitude–phase initial conditions is the cosine normal form
  `x(t) = A cos (ω t - φ)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_trajectory_eq_cos (S : HarmonicOscillator) (IC : AmplitudePhase)
    (t : Time) :
    (IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S t
      = EuclideanSpace.single 0 (IC.A * cos (S.ω * t - IC.φ))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.AmplitudePhase.toInitialConditions_velocity_eq_sin
entries.docstring: The velocity of the amplitude–phase trajectory is `v(t) = -A ω sin (ω t - φ)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_velocity_eq_sin (S : HarmonicOscillator) (IC : AmplitudePhase)
    (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ ((IC.toInitialConditions S).trajectory S) t
      = EuclideanSpace.single 0 (-(IC.A * S.ω * sin (S.ω * t.val - IC.φ)))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions
entries.docstring:
Recover amplitude–phase data from standard initial conditions, as the polar coordinates of the
  phase vector `(x₀, v₀ / ω)` embedded as `z = x₀ + (v₀ / ω) i`: the amplitude is `‖z‖` and the
  phase is `Complex.arg z`.

  See `toInitialConditions_fromInitialConditions` for the right-inverse identity.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def fromInitialConditions (S : HarmonicOscillator) (IC : InitialConditions) :
    AmplitudePhase where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.AmplitudePhase.toInitialConditions_fromInitialConditions
entries.docstring:
`fromInitialConditions` is a right inverse of `toInitialConditions`: converting initial
  conditions to amplitude–phase form and back recovers them exactly.
entries.snippet:
lemma toInitialConditions_fromInitialConditions (S : HarmonicOscillator)
    (IC : InitialConditions) :
    (fromInitialConditions S IC).toInitialConditions S = IC

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_eq_cos
entries.docstring:
Every trajectory of the harmonic oscillator is a single shifted cosine after converting its
  initial conditions to amplitude-phase form.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_cos (IC : InitialConditions) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t =
      EuclideanSpace.single 0 ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A *
        cos (S.ω * t - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_velocity_eq_sin
entries.docstring: The velocity of every trajectory is the corresponding shifted sine in amplitude-phase form.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_sin (IC : InitialConditions) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t =
      EuclideanSpace.single 0 (-((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A * S.ω *
        sin (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ)))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_sin_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the velocity vanishes exactly when the sine factor in
  amplitude-phase form vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_sin_eq_zero (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      sin (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_exists_int
entries.docstring: For nonzero amplitude, the velocity is zero exactly at phase times `φ + nπ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_exists_int (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      ∃ n : ℤ,
        (t : ℝ) =
          ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ + n * π) / S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_norm_eq_amplitude
entries.docstring: The velocity vanishes exactly when the trajectory has norm equal to the amplitude.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_norm_eq_amplitude (IC : InitialConditions)
    (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      ‖IC.trajectory S t‖ = (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_eq_zero_iff_cos_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the trajectory passes through zero exactly when the cosine factor in
  amplitude-phase form vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_zero_iff_cos_eq_zero (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t = 0 ↔
      cos (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions.trajectory_eq_zero_iff_exists_int
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the trajectory passes through zero exactly at phase times
  `φ + (2n + 1)π / 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_zero_iff_exists_int (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t = 0 ↔
      ∃ n : ℤ,
        (t : ℝ) =
          ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ + (2 * n + 1) * π / 2) / S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.return_time
entries.docstring:
Assuming that the initial coordinate and velocity are not simultaneously zero,
the time stamps when the harmonic oscillator returns to its initial coordinate and velocity is
a multiple of its period
entries.snippet:
lemma return_time (IC : InitialConditions) (non_trivial : IC.x₀ ≠ 0 ∨ IC.v₀ ≠ 0)
    (t : Time) (ht : IC.trajectory S t = IC.x₀ ∧ ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = IC.v₀) :
    ∃ n : ℤ,  (n : ℝ) * (T S) = t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.isTotalTimeDerivative_explicit
entries.docstring:
Explicit reformulation (by the chain rule):
    δL(t, q, dₜ q) = ∂F/∂t(t, q) + ⟨∇ᵣF(t, q), dₜ q⟩

    or

    δL(t, q, dₜ q) = fderiv ℝ F (t, q) (1, dₜ q)
entries.snippet:
lemma isTotalTimeDerivative_explicit {δL : Time → X → X → ℝ} :
    IsTotalTimeDerivative δL ↔  (∃ (F : Time → X → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ ↿F),
    ∀ t q v, δL t q v = fderiv ℝ ↿F (t, q) ((1 : Time), v))

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction
entries.docstring:
The creation of an electromagnetic potential from a static scalar-potential function.

If the function is distribution-bounded, it is first promoted to a distribution using
`Space.distOfFunction`. Otherwise the constructor returns zero.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction {d} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (φ : Space d → ℝ) : DistElectromagneticPotential d

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction_of_isDistBounded
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction_of_isDistBounded {d} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (φ : Space d → ℝ) (hφ : Space.IsDistBounded φ) :
    ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction c φ =
      ofStaticScalarPotential c (Space.distOfFunction φ hφ)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction_eq_zero_of_not_isDistBounded
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction_eq_zero_of_not_isDistBounded {d}
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (φ : Space d → ℝ) (hφ : ¬ Space.IsDistBounded φ) :
    ofStaticScalarPotentialFunction c φ = 0

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.distTensorDeriv_eq_sum_sum
entries.snippet:
lemma distTensorDeriv_eq_sum_sum {d} (A : DistElectromagneticPotential d)
    (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    distTensorDeriv A ε =∑ μ, ∑ ν, (SpaceTime.distDeriv μ A ε ν) •
      Lorentz.CoVector.basis μ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Lorentz.Vector.basis ν

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.distTensorDeriv_basis_repr_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma distTensorDeriv_basis_repr_apply {d} {μν : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) × (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)}
    (A : DistElectromagneticPotential d)
    (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    (Lorentz.CoVector.basis.tensorProduct Lorentz.Vector.basis).repr (distTensorDeriv A ε) μν =
    distDeriv μν.1 A ε μν.2

entries.name: Electromagnetism.DistElectromagneticPotential.toTensor_distTensorDeriv_basis_repr_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_distTensorDeriv_basis_repr_apply {d} (A : DistElectromagneticPotential d)
    (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d)
      (Fin.append ![Color.down] ![Color.up])) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensorial.toTensor (distTensorDeriv A ε)) b =
    distDeriv (b 0) A ε (b 1)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eval_eq_basis_repr
entries.docstring:
Evaluating both tensor indices of the field strength gives the coefficient in the
standard tensor-product basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eval_eq_basis_repr {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    toField {A.toFieldStrength x | [μ] [ν]}ᵀ =
    (Lorentz.CoVector.basis.tensorProduct Lorentz.Vector.basis).repr
      (A.toFieldStrength x) (μ, ν)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eval_apply
entries.docstring:
The evaluated components of the field strength tensor in terms of derivatives of the
electromagnetic potential.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eval_apply {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    toField {A.toFieldStrength x | [μ] [ν]}ᵀ =
    ∑ κ, (η μ κ * ∂_ κ A x ν - η ν κ * ∂_ κ A x μ)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eval_apply_eq_single
entries.docstring:
The evaluated components of the field strength tensor after using diagonal form of the
Minkowski metric.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eval_apply_eq_single {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    toField {A.toFieldStrength x | [μ] [ν]}ᵀ =
    η μ μ * ∂_ μ A x ν - η ν ν * ∂_ ν A x μ

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eval_eq_fieldStrengthMatrix
entries.docstring:
Index evaluation of the field strength tensor agrees with the corresponding component of
the field strength matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eval_eq_fieldStrengthMatrix {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    toField {A.toFieldStrength x | [μ] [ν]}ᵀ = A.fieldStrengthMatrix x (μ, ν)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient
entries.docstring:
The pure-gauge electromagnetic potential `A^μ = ∂^μ χ = η^{μν} ∂_ν χ` built from a
  gauge function `χ`. The metric-contracted form `∑ κ, η μ κ * ∂_ κ χ` is the definition;
  the diagonal form (which equals `η μ μ * ∂_ μ χ` since `η` is diagonal) is derived in
  `ofGradient_apply`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def ofGradient {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) : ElectromagneticPotential d where

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient_apply_sum
entries.docstring: Unfolding of the summed definition of `ofGradient`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofGradient_apply_sum {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (x : SpaceTime d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ofGradient χ x μ = ∑ κ, η μ κ * ∂_ κ χ x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient_apply
entries.docstring:
Evaluation of `ofGradient` in the diagonal form; the off-diagonal entries of `η` vanish so
  only the `κ = μ` term survives.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofGradient_apply {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (x : SpaceTime d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ofGradient χ x μ = η μ μ * ∂_ μ χ x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient_zero
entries.docstring: The pure-gauge potential built from the zero gauge function has all components zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofGradient_zero {d} (x : SpaceTime d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ofGradient (0 : SpaceTime d → ℝ) x μ = 0

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient_add
entries.docstring: `ofGradient` is additive in the gauge function (when both summands are differentiable).

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.differentiable_ofGradient
entries.docstring: The pure-gauge potential is differentiable when `χ` is `C^2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiable_ofGradient {d} {χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ} (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (ofGradient χ)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.contDiff_ofGradient
entries.docstring: The pure-gauge potential is `C^n` when `χ` is `C^{n+1}`.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_ofGradient {n} {d} {χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ} (hχ : ContDiff ℝ (n + 1) χ) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (ofGradient χ)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_ofGradient
entries.docstring: A pure-gauge potential has vanishing field strength.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_ofGradient {d} {χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ} (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ)
    (x : SpaceTime d) : (ofGradient χ).toFieldStrength x = 0

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofGradient_equivariant
entries.docstring:
`ofGradient` intertwines the Lorentz action on potentials with composition by Λ⁻¹ on the
  gauge function: `Λ • ofGradient χ = ofGradient (χ ∘ (Λ⁻¹ • ·))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofGradient_equivariant {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (hχ : Differentiable ℝ χ)
    (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    Λ • ofGradient χ = ofGradient (χ ∘ (Λ⁻¹ • ·))

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform
entries.docstring: The gauge transformation `A^μ ↦ A^μ + ∂^μ χ` of an electromagnetic potential.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def gaugeTransform {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) :
    ElectromagneticPotential d

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of `gaugeTransform`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeTransform_apply {d} (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) : gaugeTransform χ A x = A x + ofGradient χ x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_gaugeTransform
entries.docstring: The field strength tensor is invariant under gauge transformations.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_gaugeTransform {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    (gaugeTransform χ A).toFieldStrength x = A.toFieldStrength x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.fieldStrengthMatrix_gaugeTransform
entries.docstring: The field strength matrix is invariant under gauge transformations.
entries.snippet:
lemma fieldStrengthMatrix_gaugeTransform {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    (gaugeTransform χ A).fieldStrengthMatrix x = A.fieldStrengthMatrix x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform_zero
entries.docstring: Shifting by the zero gauge function is the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeTransform_zero {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) :
    gaugeTransform (0 : SpaceTime d → ℝ) A = A

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform_gaugeTransform
entries.docstring:
Two successive gauge shifts compose: shifting by χ₂ then χ₁ equals shifting by χ₁ + χ₂.
  This upgrades one-step F-invariance to invariance along any finite chain of gauge shifts.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeTransform_gaugeTransform {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (χ₁ χ₂ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (hχ₁ : Differentiable ℝ χ₁) (hχ₂ : Differentiable ℝ χ₂) :
    gaugeTransform χ₁ (gaugeTransform χ₂ A) = gaugeTransform (χ₁ + χ₂) A

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform_equivariant
entries.docstring:
Gauge transformations commute with Lorentz transformations: applying Λ and then performing
  a gauge transformation by `χ` equals performing a gauge transformation by `χ ∘ (Λ⁻¹ • ·)`
  and then applying Λ.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeTransform_equivariant {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) (hχ : Differentiable ℝ χ) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    Λ • gaugeTransform χ A = gaugeTransform (χ ∘ (Λ⁻¹ • ·)) (Λ • A)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.fieldStrengthMatrix_bareGradient_inl_inr
entries.docstring:
The `(inl 0, inr i)` component of the field strength matrix of the bare-gradient potential
  `B^μ := ∂_μ χ` for `χ(x) = x⁰·xⁱ` equals `2`. This witnesses that the bare covariant gradient
  does not produce a gauge-invariant field strength, so the raised-index contraction
  `η^{μν} ∂_ν χ` in `ofGradient` is necessary (see the module overview).
entries.snippet:
lemma fieldStrengthMatrix_bareGradient_inl_inr {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) :
    let χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_bareGradient_ne_zero
entries.docstring:
The field strength of the bare-gradient potential `B^μ := ∂_μ χ` for
  `χ(x) = x⁰·xⁱ` is nonzero (follows from `fieldStrengthMatrix_bareGradient_inl_inr`).
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_bareGradient_ne_zero {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) :
    let χ : SpaceTime d → ℝ

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.magneticField_coord_eq_fieldStrengthMatrix
entries.snippet:
lemma magneticField_coord_eq_fieldStrengthMatrix {i : Fin 3} {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential) (t : Time)
    (x : Space) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) :
    A.magneticField c t x i =
    - A.fieldStrengthMatrix ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x)) (Sum.inr (i+1), Sum.inr (i+2))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.weightedDirDeriv
entries.docstring:
The base-point field `p ↦ (1/2)(d_{b₁} f + c·d_{b₂} f)`, a weighted combination of the
real Fréchet derivative of `f` along two directions `b₁`, `b₂`. The directional Wirtinger
operators are its two specializations: `dWirtingerDir f v` at `c = -i`, `(b₁, b₂) = (v, i·v)`,
and `dWirtingerAntiDir f v` at `c = i`. Keeping `b₁`, `b₂` free lets §G differentiate it a
second time once and reuse the bridge for both operators.
entries.snippet: def weightedDirDeriv (f : V → ℂ) (c : ℂ) (b₁ b₂ : V) : V → ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir
entries.docstring:
The holomorphic directional Wirtinger derivative `∂_v f = (1/2)(d_v f − i·d_{i·v} f)`
of `f : V → ℂ` along the direction vector `v : V`, the `weightedDirDeriv` at `c = -i`.
entries.snippet: def dWirtingerDir (f : V → ℂ) (v u : V) : ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir
entries.docstring:
The anti-holomorphic directional Wirtinger derivative
`∂̄_v f = (1/2)(d_v f + i·d_{i·v} f)` of `f : V → ℂ` along the direction vector `v : V`,
the `weightedDirDeriv` at `c = i`.
entries.snippet: def dWirtingerAntiDir (f : V → ℂ) (v u : V) : ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_apply
entries.docstring:
Definitional unfolding of `dWirtingerDir` to the explicit Wirtinger combination, used to
expand the outer operator of a composition without touching the inner one.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_apply (g : V → ℂ) (v u : V) :
    dWirtingerDir g v u
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ g u v - Complex.I * fderiv ℝ g u (Complex.I • v))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_apply
entries.docstring: Definitional unfolding of `dWirtingerAntiDir` to the explicit Wirtinger combination.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_apply (g : V → ℂ) (v u : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir g v u
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ g u v + Complex.I * fderiv ℝ g u (Complex.I • v))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_add
entries.docstring: Additivity of `dWirtingerDir`, `∂_v(g + h) = ∂_v g + ∂_v h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_add {g h : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (g + h) v u = dWirtingerDir g v u + dWirtingerDir h v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_add
entries.docstring: Additivity of `dWirtingerAntiDir`, `∂̄_v(g + h) = ∂̄_v g + ∂̄_v h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_add {g h : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (g + h) v u = dWirtingerAntiDir g v u + dWirtingerAntiDir h v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_smul
entries.docstring:
Compatibility of `dWirtingerDir` with complex scalar multiplication,
`∂_v(c·g) = c·∂_v g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_smul (c : ℂ) {g : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (c • g) v u = c • dWirtingerDir g v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_smul
entries.docstring:
Compatibility of `dWirtingerAntiDir` with complex scalar multiplication,
`∂̄_v(c·g) = c·∂̄_v g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_smul (c : ℂ) {g : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (c • g) v u = c • dWirtingerAntiDir g v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_mul_apply
entries.docstring: The real Fréchet derivative of a product, evaluated at a tangent `v`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_mul
entries.docstring:
The Wirtinger Leibniz rule for `dWirtingerDir`,
`∂_v(g·h) = ∂_v g·h + g·∂_v h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_mul {g h : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (g * h) v u = dWirtingerDir g v u * h u + g u * dWirtingerDir h v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_mul
entries.docstring:
The Wirtinger Leibniz rule for `dWirtingerAntiDir`,
`∂̄_v(g·h) = ∂̄_v g·h + g·∂̄_v h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_mul {g h : V → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (g * h) v u =
      dWirtingerAntiDir g v u * h u + g u * dWirtingerAntiDir h v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_fun_sum
entries.docstring: Finite-sum rule for `dWirtingerDir`, `∂_v(∑ₐ Fₐ) = ∑ₐ ∂_v Fₐ`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_fun_sum
entries.docstring: Finite-sum rule for `dWirtingerAntiDir`, `∂̄_v(∑ₐ Fₐ) = ∑ₐ ∂̄_v Fₐ`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_star_eq
entries.docstring:
Differentiation commutes with conjugation: the real Fréchet derivative of the
pointwise conjugate `p ↦ star (f p)` is `conjCLE` (conjugation on `ℂ`) composed with
`fderiv ℝ f u`; in physicists' notation, `d f̄ = conj(d f)`. Conjugation is `ℝ`-linear,
so it slides through the real derivative unchanged, whereas it does *not* commute with
the holomorphic Wirtinger derivative `∂_v`. The `star` conjugates the *output* `f p`,
so this is not a derivative in a conjugate variable.

This is the analytic core of the conjugation lemmas below
(`dWirtingerDir_star_comp` and its dual): distributed over the Wirtinger split of
`fderiv ℝ f u` (`realLinear_apply_eq_wirtinger`, §D), the outer `conjCLE` conjugates the two
coefficients and swaps the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic parts.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_star_eq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {f : E → ℂ} {u : E} (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun p : E => star (f p)) u =
      Complex.conjCLE.toContinuousLinearMap.comp (fderiv ℝ f u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_star_comp
entries.docstring:
Conjugating the function swaps the operators up to an outer conjugation:
`∂_v f̄ = conj (∂̄_v f)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_star_comp (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (fun p => star (f p)) v u = star (dWirtingerAntiDir f v u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_star_comp
entries.docstring:
Conjugating the function swaps the operators up to an outer conjugation:
`∂̄_v f̄ = conj (∂_v f)`. Dual of `dWirtingerDir_star_comp`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_star_comp (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (fun p => star (f p)) v u = star (dWirtingerDir f v u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.realLinear_apply_eq_wirtinger
entries.docstring:
Split a real-linear map `ℂ → ℂ` into its Wirtinger components. Any
real-linear `L : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ` splits into a holomorphic and an anti-holomorphic part
with the Wirtinger coefficients `a = ½(L 1 - i * L i)`, `b = ½(L 1 + i * L i)` as
weights:

  `L w = a * w + b * star w`.

This is purely algebraic: `L` is an arbitrary real-linear map, no derivative
involved. Its use is the Wirtinger chain rule (`dWirtingerDir_comp` below), where the
weights of the outer differential `L = fderiv ℝ g (f u)` are the coefficients `∂g/∂f`,
`∂g/∂f̄`.
entries.snippet:
lemma realLinear_apply_eq_wirtinger (L : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ) (w : ℂ) :
    L w =
      ((1 / 2 : ℂ) * (L 1 - Complex.I * L Complex.I)) * w
        + ((1 / 2 : ℂ) * (L 1 + Complex.I * L Complex.I)) * star w

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_comp
entries.docstring:
The two-term Wirtinger chain rule for `dWirtingerDir`, outer `g : ℂ → ℂ` and inner
`f : V → ℂ`:

  `∂_v(g∘f) = (∂g/∂f)·∂_v f + (∂g/∂f̄)·∂_v f̄`.

`realLinear_apply_eq_wirtinger` splits the chain rule's outer `ℝ`-linear factor into the
`∂g/∂f`, `∂g/∂f̄` coefficients, each multiplying its inner directional derivative `∂_v f`,
`∂_v f̄`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_comp {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (f u))
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (fun p => g (f p)) v u =
      dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerDir f v u
        + dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerDir (fun p => star (f p)) v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_comp
entries.docstring:
The two-term Wirtinger chain rule for `dWirtingerAntiDir`, the anti-holomorphic dual of
`dWirtingerDir_comp`:

  `∂̄_v(g∘f) = (∂g/∂f)·∂̄_v f + (∂g/∂f̄)·∂̄_v f̄`.

Same outer `∂g/∂f`, `∂g/∂f̄` coefficients, now each multiplying its anti-holomorphic inner
derivative `∂̄_v f`, `∂̄_v f̄`; same proof as `dWirtingerDir_comp`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_comp {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (f u))
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (fun p => g (f p)) v u =
      dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerAntiDir f v u
        + dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerAntiDir (fun p => star (f p)) v u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_comp_clm_apply
entries.docstring:
Chain rule for an inner continuous linear map `L`. Because the derivative of a linear
map is the map itself, the real Fréchet derivative of `g ∘ L` at `u`, applied to `x`, equals
the derivative of `g` at `L u` applied to `L x`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_comp_conjLinear
entries.docstring:
Domain conjugation swaps the operators: precomposing with a conjugate-`ℂ`-linear `L`
turns the holomorphic derivative of `g ∘ L` at `u` into the anti-holomorphic derivative of
`g` at the mapped point `L u`, in the mapped direction `L v`:
`∂_v(g ∘ L)` at `u` equals `∂̄_{L v} g` at `L u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerDir_comp_conjLinear {g : V' → ℂ} {L : V →L[ℝ] V'} {u : V}
    (hL : ∀ x : V, L (Complex.I • x) = -(Complex.I • L x))
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (L u)) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (fun p => g (L p)) v u = dWirtingerAntiDir g (L v) (L u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_comp_conjLinear
entries.docstring:
Dual of `dWirtingerDir_comp_conjLinear`: the anti-holomorphic derivative of `g ∘ L` at
`u` is the holomorphic derivative of `g` at the mapped point `L u`, in the mapped direction
`L v`: `∂̄_v(g ∘ L)` at `u` equals `∂_{L v} g` at `L u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_comp_conjLinear {g : V' → ℂ} {L : V →L[ℝ] V'} {u : V}
    (hL : ∀ x : V, L (Complex.I • x) = -(Complex.I • L x))
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (L u)) (v : V) :
    dWirtingerAntiDir (fun p => g (L p)) v u = dWirtingerDir g (L v) (L u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_eq_of_clinear
entries.docstring:
Holomorphic collapse: along a direction where the real derivative is `ℂ`-linear, the
holomorphic derivative is the full real derivative, `∂_v f = d_v f`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero_of_clinear
entries.docstring:
Holomorphic collapse: the anti-holomorphic derivative vanishes along a direction
of `ℂ`-linearity, `∂̄_v f = 0`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_eq_zero_of_antilinear
entries.docstring:
Anti-holomorphic collapse: a direction of conjugate-`ℂ`-linearity kills the
holomorphic derivative, `∂_v f = 0`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_of_antilinear
entries.docstring:
Anti-holomorphic collapse: the anti-holomorphic derivative is the full real
derivative along a direction of conjugate-`ℂ`-linearity, `∂̄_v f = d_v f`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hasFDerivAt_fderiv_apply
entries.docstring:
The field `p ↦ d_b f` is the evaluation map `· b` composed with `fderiv ℝ f`,
so when `fderiv ℝ f` is differentiable its derivative is `fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u`
post-composed with that evaluation.
entries.snippet:
private lemma hasFDerivAt_fderiv_apply (hf' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
    (b : V) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun p => fderiv ℝ f p b)
      ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℂ b).comp (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hasFDerivAt_weightedDirDeriv
entries.docstring: The `weightedDirDeriv` is differentiable wherever `fderiv ℝ f` is.
entries.snippet:
private lemma hasFDerivAt_weightedDirDeriv (hf' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
    (c : ℂ) (b₁ b₂ : V) :
    HasFDerivAt (weightedDirDeriv f c b₁ b₂)
      ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℂ b₁).comp (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
        + c • (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℂ b₂).comp (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u))) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_weightedDirDeriv
entries.docstring:
The bridge: differentiating a `weightedDirDeriv` along a third direction `a`
lands on the second real Fréchet derivative `fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a b` in the
two slots.
entries.snippet:
private lemma fderiv_weightedDirDeriv (hf' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
    (c : ℂ) (b₁ b₂ a : V) :
    fderiv ℝ (weightedDirDeriv f c b₁ b₂) u a
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a b₁
          + c * fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a b₂)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_weightedDirDeriv
entries.docstring: A directional derivative is a `weightedDirDeriv`: anti-holomorphic with `c = i`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_weightedDirDeriv (w : V) :
    (fun p => dWirtingerAntiDir f w p) = weightedDirDeriv f Complex.I w (Complex.I • w)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_eq_weightedDirDeriv
entries.docstring: A directional derivative is a `weightedDirDeriv`: holomorphic with `c = -i`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma dWirtingerDir_eq_weightedDirDeriv (v : V) :
    (fun p => dWirtingerDir f v p) = weightedDirDeriv f (-Complex.I) v (Complex.I • v)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_dWirtingerAntiDir
entries.docstring:
Differentiating the anti-holomorphic directional derivative lands on the second
real Fréchet derivative in the two slots.
entries.snippet:
private lemma fderiv_dWirtingerAntiDir (hf' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
    (w a : V) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun p => dWirtingerAntiDir f w p) u a
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a w
          + Complex.I * fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a (Complex.I • w))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_dWirtingerDir
entries.docstring:
Differentiating the holomorphic directional derivative lands on the second real
Fréchet derivative in the two slots.
entries.snippet:
private lemma fderiv_dWirtingerDir (hf' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u)
    (v a : V) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun p => dWirtingerDir f v p) u a
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a v
          - Complex.I * fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u a (Complex.I • v))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerDir
entries.docstring:
On a `C²` field the holomorphic directional derivative is itself
real-differentiable.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerDir (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (v : V) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p => dWirtingerDir f v p) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiDir
entries.docstring:
On a `C²` field the anti-holomorphic directional derivative is itself
real-differentiable.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiDir (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (w : V) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p => dWirtingerAntiDir f w p) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_congr_of_eventuallyEq
entries.docstring:
The holomorphic directional derivative depends only on the field near the point:
fields agreeing on a neighbourhood have equal derivative.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiDir_congr_of_eventuallyEq
entries.docstring:
The anti-holomorphic directional derivative depends only on the field near the
point; dual of `dWirtingerDir_congr_of_eventuallyEq`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerDir_dWirtingerAntiDir_comm
entries.docstring:
**Schwarz's theorem** for the directional Wirtinger operators: on a `C²` field `f` the
holomorphic and anti-holomorphic directional derivatives commute in any two directions,
`∂_v ∂̄_w f = ∂̄_w ∂_v f`.

The commutation adds no analytic input. By the §G bridge each order expands into a real-linear
combination of the second real Fréchet derivative `fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) u` on the four
directions `v`, `i·v`, `w`, `i·w`. The two orders give the same combination up to transposing
the two slots of that second derivative, and `ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt`, the symmetry of
ordinary mixed second partials, equates them.
entries.snippet:
theorem dWirtingerDir_dWirtingerAntiDir_comm (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (v w : V) :
    dWirtingerDir (fun p => dWirtingerAntiDir f w p) v u
      = dWirtingerAntiDir (fun p => dWirtingerDir f v p) w u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord
entries.docstring: Holomorphic Wirtinger derivative along the I-th coordinate of `ι → ℂ`.
entries.snippet: def dWirtingerCoord (f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ) (I : ι) : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord
entries.docstring: Anti-holomorphic Wirtinger derivative along the I-th coordinate of `ι → ℂ`.
entries.snippet: def dWirtingerAntiCoord (f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ) (I : ι) : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_apply
entries.docstring:
Real-Fréchet form of `dWirtingerCoord`:
`dWirtingerCoord f I u = (1/2)(∂_x − i · ∂_y) f`,
the derivatives along the slot-I real and imaginary coordinate directions.
Unconditional — the directional definition makes it definitional
(`Complex.I • Pi.single I 1 = Pi.single I Complex.I`); no differentiability
hypothesis is needed.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_apply {f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ}
    {u : (ι → ℂ)} (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord f I u = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single I 1)
      - Complex.I * fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single I Complex.I))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_apply
entries.docstring:
Real-Fréchet form of `dWirtingerAntiCoord`:
`∂̄_I f = (1/2)(∂_x + i · ∂_y) f`,
mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_apply` with the sign flip on the imaginary-direction term.
Unconditional, as for `dWirtingerCoord_apply`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_apply {f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ}
    {u : (ι → ℂ)} (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u = (1 / 2 : ℂ) * (fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single I 1)
      + Complex.I * fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single I Complex.I))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.clinear_of_holomorphic
entries.docstring:
The real derivative of a holomorphic `f : E → ℂ` is `ℂ`-linear along every direction —
the hypothesis the foundation collapse `dWirtingerDir_eq_of_clinear` consumes. A holomorphic
`f` has `fderiv ℝ f u = (fderiv ℂ f u).restrictScalars ℝ`
(`DifferentiableAt.fderiv_restrictScalars`), so its real derivative agrees with the `ℂ`-linear
complex derivative on every direction. Used at `E = ι → ℂ` for the coordinate collapse and at
`E = ℂ` for the outer-`g` chain rule (§D).
entries.snippet:
private lemma clinear_of_holomorphic {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedSpace ℂ E] [IsScalarTower ℝ ℂ E] {f : E → ℂ} {u : E}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℂ f u) (d : E) :
    fderiv ℝ f u (Complex.I • d) = Complex.I • fderiv ℝ f u d

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_congr_of_eventuallyEq_apply
entries.docstring:
`dWirtingerCoord` is local: functions agreeing on a neighbourhood of `u` have equal
holomorphic Wirtinger derivative at `u` (`f₁ =ᶠ[nhds u] f₂ ⟹ ∂_I f₁ u = ∂_I f₂ u`).

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_neg_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise negation rule for the holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂_I (−f) = −∂_I f`. Used with `dWirtingerCoord_add_apply` to assemble the
coordinate-difference rule `dWirtingerCoord_coordDiff` (§C).
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_neg_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)} (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => -(f v)) I u = -(dWirtingerCoord f I u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.fderiv_coordProj
entries.docstring:
The real Fréchet derivative of the J-th coordinate projection `v ↦ v J`. Consumed by the
Kronecker coordinate-value lemmas `dWirtingerCoord_coordProj` / `dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordProj`,
which feed it the slot-I real and imaginary directions.
entries.snippet:
private lemma fderiv_coordProj (J : ι) (u d : (ι → ℂ)) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => v J) u d = d J

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_add_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise additivity of the holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂_I (f + g) = ∂_I f + ∂_I g`. Used to assemble the coordinate-difference rule
`dWirtingerCoord_coordDiff` (§C).

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_smul_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise compatibility with complex scalar multiplication at `u`:
`∂_I (c • f) = c • ∂_I f`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_mul_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise Leibniz rule for the holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂_I (f · g) = ∂_I f · g + f · ∂_I g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_mul_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (f * g) I u =
      dWirtingerCoord f I u * g u + f u * dWirtingerCoord g I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_fun_sum_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise finite-sum rule for holomorphic coordinate derivatives at `u`:
`∂_I (∑ a ∈ s, F a) = ∑ a ∈ s, ∂_I (F a)`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_eq_complex_fderiv_apply
entries.docstring:
For a holomorphic function, `dWirtingerCoord` is the complex Fréchet derivative in
the corresponding coordinate direction: `∂_I f = fderiv ℂ f u (Pi.single I 1)`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.conjCLM
entries.docstring:
Pointwise conjugation bundled as an ℝ-linear CLM (conjugate-ℂ-linear): the I-th
component is conjugation of the I-th coordinate `Complex.conjCLE ∘ proj I`. Its underlying
function is the `star` of `ι → ℂ` (`conjCLM_apply`). Bundling `star` as a `→L[ℝ]` is what
lets the anti-holomorphic lemmas below feed it to the foundation `dWirtingerDir_comp_conjLinear`,
which requires its domain map as a continuous linear map.
entries.snippet: private def conjCLM : (ι → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι → ℂ)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.conjCLM_smul_I
entries.docstring:
`conjCLM` is conjugate-ℂ-linear: `conj (i·d) = -(i · conj d)`. The `hL` hypothesis the
foundation `dWirtingerDir_comp_conjLinear` / `dWirtingerAntiDir_comp_conjLinear` consume.
entries.snippet:
private lemma conjCLM_smul_I (d : ι → ℂ) :
    conjCLM (Complex.I • d) = -(Complex.I • conjCLM (ι := ι) d)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_eq_zero_of_antiHolomorphic_apply
entries.docstring:
An *anti-holomorphic* function `v ↦ g (star v)` (a holomorphic `g` precomposed
with conjugation) depends on the coordinates only through their conjugates `z̄`. Its
holomorphic derivative therefore vanishes, `∂_I (g ∘ star) = 0`, since `∂_I`
differentiates w.r.t. `z` and treats `z̄` as constant. Dual to `∂̄_I f = 0` for
holomorphic `f`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_congr_of_eventuallyEq_apply
entries.docstring: `dWirtingerAntiCoord` is local (`f₁ =ᶠ[nhds u] f₂ ⟹ ∂̄_I f₁ u = ∂̄_I f₂ u`).

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_neg_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise negation rule for the anti-holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂̄_I (−f) = −∂̄_I f`. Used with `dWirtingerAntiCoord_add_apply` to assemble the
coordinate-difference rule `dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordDiff` (§C).
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_neg_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)} (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => -(f v)) I u = -(dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_conjCoord
entries.docstring:
`∂_I z̄^J = 0`. The conjugate of `dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordProj` (`z̄^J = star z^J`),
read off through `dWirtingerDir_star_comp` rather than recomputed. Used to assemble the
coordinate-difference rule `dWirtingerCoord_coordDiff` (§C).
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_conjCoord (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun u : (ι → ℂ) => star (u J)) I = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_conjCoord
entries.docstring:
`∂̄_I z̄^J = δ_IJ`. The conjugate of `dWirtingerCoord_coordProj`, read off through
`dWirtingerAntiDir_star_comp` rather than recomputed. Used to assemble the
coordinate-difference rule `dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordDiff` (§C).
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_conjCoord (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun u : (ι → ℂ) => star (u J)) I =
      fun _ => if I = J then 1 else 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_add_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise additivity of the anti-holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂̄_I (f + g) = ∂̄_I f + ∂̄_I g`. Used to assemble the coordinate-difference rule
`dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordDiff` (§C).

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_smul_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise compatibility with complex scalar multiplication at `u`:
`∂̄_I (c • f) = c • ∂̄_I f`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_mul_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise Leibniz rule for the anti-holomorphic coordinate derivative at `u`:
`∂̄_I (f · g) = ∂̄_I f · g + f · ∂̄_I g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_mul_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (f * g) I u =
      dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u * g u + f u * dWirtingerAntiCoord g I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_fun_sum_apply
entries.docstring:
Pointwise finite-sum rule for anti-holomorphic coordinate derivatives at `u`:
`∂̄_I (∑ a ∈ s, F a) = ∑ a ∈ s, ∂̄_I (F a)`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_eq_complex_fderiv_apply
entries.docstring:
For an anti-holomorphic function the anti-holomorphic Wirtinger derivative equals
the complex Fréchet derivative of `g` at `star u` along the slot-I real
coordinate direction, `∂̄_I (g ∘ star) = fderiv ℂ g (star u) (Pi.single I 1)`.
Dual of `dWirtingerCoord_eq_complex_fderiv_apply`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_eq_complex_fderiv_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g (star u)) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => g (star v)) I u =
      fderiv ℂ g (star u) (Pi.single I 1)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_eq_zero_of_holomorphic_apply
entries.docstring: Holomorphic functions have zero anti-holomorphic coordinate derivative: `∂̄_I f = 0`.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.coordDiff_eq_add_neg
entries.docstring:
The coordinate difference `z^J − z̄^J` as a sum of the holomorphic coordinate
and the negated conjugate coordinate — the form on which the `dWirtingerCoord` /
`dWirtingerAntiCoord` additivity rules apply.

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_coordDiff
entries.docstring:
`∂_I (z^J − z̄^J) = δ_IJ`, from `∂_I z^J = δ_IJ` and
`∂_I z̄^J = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_coordDiff (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => v J - star (v J)) I
      = fun _ => if I = J then 1 else 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordDiff
entries.docstring:
`∂̄_I (z^J − z̄^J) = −δ_IJ`, from `∂̄_I z^J = 0` and
`∂̄_I z̄^J = δ_IJ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_coordDiff (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => v J - star (v J)) I
      = fun _ => if I = J then -1 else 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_apply
entries.docstring:
The two-term coordinate chain rule for a real-differentiable outer `g`, pointwise at `u`:
`∂_I (g ∘ f) = (∂g/∂f) · ∂_I f + (∂g/∂f̄) · ∂_I f̄`,
with coefficients `∂g/∂f = dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u)` and `∂g/∂f̄ = dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u)`.
The `d = Pi.single I 1` case of the foundation `dWirtingerDir_comp`. The single-term
holomorphic specialization `dWirtingerCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply` is proved from this.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (f u)) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => g (f v)) I u =
      dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerCoord f I u
        + dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u) *
          dWirtingerCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => star (f v)) I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply
entries.docstring:
The single-term coordinate chain rule for a holomorphic outer `g`, pointwise at `u`:
`∂_I (g ∘ f) = deriv g (f u) · ∂_I f`. From the two-term `dWirtingerCoord_comp_apply`: for
holomorphic `g` the anti-holomorphic coefficient `dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u)` vanishes and
`dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u)` collapses to `deriv g (f u)`, both off the `ℂ`-linearity
`clinear_of_holomorphic` (§B).
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g (f u)) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => g (f v)) I u =
      deriv g (f u) * dWirtingerCoord f I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_star_comp_apply
entries.docstring:
Conjugating the inner field swaps the two operators: `∂_I f̄ = conj (∂̄_I f)`. The
`d = Pi.single I 1` case of the foundation `dWirtingerDir_star_comp`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_star_comp_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => star (f v)) I u =
      star (dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_apply
entries.docstring:
The two-term coordinate chain rule for a real-differentiable outer `g`, anti-holomorphic
version, pointwise at `u`: `∂̄_I (g ∘ f) = (∂g/∂f) · ∂̄_I f + (∂g/∂f̄) · ∂̄_I f̄`. Same outer
coefficients as `dWirtingerCoord_comp_apply`, now multiplying the anti-holomorphic inner
derivatives. The `d = Pi.single I 1` case of the foundation `dWirtingerAntiDir_comp`. The
single-term holomorphic specialization `dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply` is proved
from this.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (f u)) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => g (f v)) I u =
      dWirtingerDir g 1 (f u) * dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u
        + dWirtingerAntiDir g 1 (f u) *
          dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => star (f v)) I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply
entries.docstring:
The single-term coordinate chain rule for a holomorphic outer `g`, anti-holomorphic
version, pointwise at `u`: `∂̄_I (g ∘ f) = deriv g (f u) · ∂̄_I f`. As in
`dWirtingerCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply`, the `∂g/∂f̄` channel vanishes and `∂g/∂f`
collapses to `deriv g (f u)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g (f u)) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => g (f v)) I u =
      deriv g (f u) * dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_star_comp_apply
entries.docstring:
Conjugating the inner field swaps the two operators: `∂̄_I f̄ = conj (∂_I f)`. Dual of
`dWirtingerCoord_star_comp_apply`, the `d = Pi.single I 1` case of the foundation
`dWirtingerAntiDir_star_comp`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_star_comp_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => star (f v)) I u =
      star (dWirtingerCoord f I u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerCoord
entries.docstring:
On a `C²` function the holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative is itself
real-differentiable (`DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂_I f) u`) — the `d = Pi.single I 1` case of
`differentiableAt_dWirtingerDir`.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerCoord (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (I : ι) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun v => dWirtingerCoord f I v) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiCoord
entries.docstring:
On a `C²` function the anti-holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative is itself
real-differentiable (`DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂̄_J f) u`) — the `d = Pi.single J 1` case of
`differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiDir`.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiCoord (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (J : ι) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun v => dWirtingerAntiCoord f J v) u

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_dWirtingerAntiCoord_comm
entries.docstring:
**Schwarz's theorem** for the coordinate Wirtinger operators: on a `C²` function the
holomorphic and anti-holomorphic derivatives commute, `∂_I ∂̄_J f = ∂̄_J ∂_I f`. The
`d = Pi.single I 1`, `e = Pi.single J 1` case of the general
`dWirtingerDir_dWirtingerAntiDir_comm`.
entries.snippet:
theorem dWirtingerCoord_dWirtingerAntiCoord_comm (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => dWirtingerAntiCoord f J v) I u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => dWirtingerCoord f I v) J u

entries.name: ConjModule
entries.docstring:
The conjugate module of `M`: the same additive group with the scalar action twisted by
conjugation, `r • v = star r • v`. A type synonym so the twisted action stays off `M`.
entries.snippet: def ConjModule (M : Type*)

entries.name: ConjModule.«instance@88e8497f»
entries.snippet: instance : AddCommGroup (ConjModule M)

entries.name: ConjModule.instModule
entries.docstring:
The twisted action `r • v = star r • v`, obtained by restricting scalars along the
conjugation ring endomorphism `starRingEnd k`.
entries.snippet: instance instModule : Module k (ConjModule M)

entries.name: conjEquiv
entries.docstring:
The canonical conjugate-linear equivalence `M ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] ConjModule M`, the identity on
the underlying additive group.
entries.snippet: def conjEquiv : M ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] ConjModule M where

entries.name: ConjModule.involution
entries.docstring:
Conjugating twice returns the original module: the `k`-linear isomorphism
`ConjModule (ConjModule M) ≃ₗ[k] M`. It is `k`-linear, not merely semilinear, because
`starRingEnd k` composed with itself is the identity.
entries.snippet: def involution : ConjModule (ConjModule M) ≃ₗ[k] M

entries.name: ConjModule.starFinsupp
entries.docstring: Coordinate-wise conjugation on `ι →₀ k`, a conjugate-linear self-equivalence.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def starFinsupp : (ι →₀ k) ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] (ι →₀ k) where

entries.name: Basis.conj
entries.docstring:
A basis of `M` transported to a basis of `ConjModule M`: the same basis vectors, with
coordinates conjugated (`(Basis.conj b).repr v = star ∘ b.repr v`).
entries.snippet: noncomputable def _root_.Basis.conj (b : Basis ι k M) : Basis ι k (ConjModule M)

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductMatrix
entries.docstring:
The hat map `[ω]ₓ`: the skew-symmetric `3 × 3` matrix acting as the cross product with `ω`,
i.e. `[ω]ₓ *ᵥ v = ω ⨯₃ v`.
entries.snippet: def crossProductMatrix (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductMatrix_mulVec
entries.docstring: The hat matrix acts on a vector as the cross product.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma crossProductMatrix_mulVec (ω v : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    crossProductMatrix ω *ᵥ v = ω ⨯₃ v

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductMatrix_transpose
entries.docstring: The hat map produces skew-symmetric matrices.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma crossProductMatrix_transpose (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    (crossProductMatrix ω)ᵀ = - crossProductMatrix ω

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductVee
entries.docstring: The vee map: reads the vector off a `3 × 3` matrix. It is a left inverse of the hat map.
entries.snippet: def crossProductVee (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductVee_crossProductMatrix
entries.docstring: The vee map is a left inverse of the hat map.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma crossProductVee_crossProductMatrix (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    crossProductVee (crossProductMatrix ω) = ω

entries.name: KroneckerDelta.generalizedKroneckerDelta
entries.docstring:
Generalized Kronecker delta:
`δ^{μ₁...μₙ}_{ν₁...νₙ} = det (δ[μᵢ, νⱼ])`.

This is defined for any finite type `α` with decidable equality.
entries.snippet:
def generalizedKroneckerDelta {α ι : Type} [DecidableEq α]
    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]
    (μ : ι → α) (ν : ι → α) : ℤ

entries.name: KroneckerDelta.generalizedKroneckerDelta_swap
entries.docstring:
Swapping two of the upper indices of the generalized Kronecker delta negates it.
This is one row transposition of the underlying determinant.
entries.snippet:
lemma generalizedKroneckerDelta_swap {α ι : Type} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]
    (μ ν : ι → α) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    generalizedKroneckerDelta (μ ∘ Equiv.swap i j) ν = - generalizedKroneckerDelta μ ν

entries.name: LinearPMap.sub_le_zero
entries.snippet: lemma sub_le_zero : f - f ≤ 0

entries.name: LinearPMap.neg_add_le_zero
entries.snippet: lemma neg_add_le_zero : -f + f ≤ 0

entries.name: LinearPMap.le_iff_neg_le_neg
entries.snippet: lemma le_iff_neg_le_neg : g₁ ≤ g₂ ↔ -g₁ ≤ -g₂

lemma mem_subgroup_iff_quotientMap_eq_one (q : GaugeGroupQuot) (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    g ∈ subgroup q ↔ quotientMap q g = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupQuot.quotientMap_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two representatives have the same image under the selected quotient map exactly when their
quotient lies in the subgroup selected by the quotient choice.
entries.snippet:
lemma quotientMap_eq_iff (q : GaugeGroupQuot) (g h : GaugeGroupI) :
    quotientMap q g = quotientMap q h ↔ g / h ∈ subgroup q

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealScalars
entries.docstring: The underlying real values of the Higgs vector.
entries.snippet: def toRealScalars : HiggsVec →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 4 → ℝ) where

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealScalars_smul_real
entries.snippet:
lemma toRealScalars_smul_real (a : ℝ) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    toRealScalars (a • φ) = a • toRealScalars φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal_toRealScalars
entries.snippet:
lemma ofReal_toRealScalars (a : ℝ) :
    toRealScalars (ofReal a) = !₄[Real.sqrt a, 0, 0, 0]

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal_toRealScalars_norm
entries.snippet:
lemma ofReal_toRealScalars_norm (φ : HiggsVec) :
    toRealScalars (ofReal (‖φ‖ ^ 2)) = !₄[‖φ‖, 0, 0, 0]

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential
entries.docstring: A general potential of the Higgs field.
entries.snippet: abbrev EffectivePotential : Type

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant
entries.docstring:
The proposition that the general potential is invariant under
  the global action of the gauge group.
entries.snippet: def IsInvariant (V : EffectivePotential) : Prop

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.eq_on_orbits
entries.docstring: An invariant potential is equal on gauge orbits.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_on_orbits {φ1 φ2 : HiggsVec} {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V)
    (hφ : φ1 ∈ MulAction.orbit GaugeGroupI  φ2) :
    V φ1 = V φ2

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.eq_of_norm_eq
entries.docstring: An invariant potential is equal on Higgs vectors with identical norms.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_norm_eq {φ1 φ2 : HiggsVec} {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V)
    (hφ : ‖φ1‖ = ‖φ2‖) :
    V φ1 = V φ2

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.factors_through_norm
entries.snippet:
lemma factors_through_norm {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V) :
    ∃ (f : ℝ → ℝ), V = f ∘ norm

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.HasMaxMassDimLE
entries.docstring:
The proposition that the potential `V` has a maximum mass dimension
  less then or equal to `n` - also implying it is a polynomial.
entries.snippet: def HasMaxMassDimLE (V : EffectivePotential) (n : ℕ) : Prop

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.polynomial
entries.docstring:
The polynomial associated to a potential `V` with a maximum mass dimension
  less than or equal to `n`.
entries.snippet:
def polynomial (V : EffectivePotential) {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin 4) ℝ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.polynomial_totalDegree
entries.snippet:
lemma polynomial_totalDegree {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    (polynomial V h).totalDegree ≤ n

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_polynomial
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_polynomial {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) : V φ = (polynomial V h).eval φ.toRealScalars

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim
entries.docstring: The part of a potential at a given mass-dimension.
entries.snippet:
def termOfMassDim (V : EffectivePotential) {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ) :
    HiggsVec → ℝ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_eq_zero_of_max_lt
entries.snippet:
lemma termOfMassDim_eq_zero_of_max_lt {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    {m : ℕ} (hm : n < m) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    termOfMassDim V h m φ = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_homogeneity
entries.snippet:
lemma termOfMassDim_homogeneity {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ)
    (φ : HiggsVec) (t : ℝ) : termOfMassDim V h m (t • φ) = t ^ m * termOfMassDim V h m φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_termOfMassDim
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_sum_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), termOfMassDim V h m φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_smul_eq_sum_termOfMassDim
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_smul_eq_sum_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) (t : ℝ) :
    V (t • φ) = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), t ^ m * termOfMassDim V h m φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_isInvariant
entries.snippet:
lemma termOfMassDim_isInvariant {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (m : ℕ) (hV : IsInvariant V) : IsInvariant (termOfMassDim V h m)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_eq_mul_norm
StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_zero_of_odd
entries.snippet:
lemma termOfMassDim_zero_of_odd {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) (hodd : Odd m)  :
    termOfMassDim V h m φ = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1), termOfMassDim V h (2 * m) φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim_fin
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim_fin {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m : Fin (n/2 + 1), termOfMassDim V h (2 * m) φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_norm_pow
entries.docstring: The potential is equal to the sum of norms to even powers.
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_sum_norm_pow {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ∃ c : Fin (n/2 + 1) → ℝ, V φ = ∑ m, c m • ‖φ‖ ^ (2 * m.1)

entries.name: MSSMCharges.sum_MSSMSpecies_numberCharges_eq_expand
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_MSSMSpecies_numberCharges_eq_expand [AddCommMonoid M]
    (f : Fin MSSMSpecies.numberCharges → M) :
    ∑ i, f i = f ⟨0, by simp⟩ + f ⟨1, by simp⟩ + f ⟨2, by simp⟩

entries.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralScalarConfiguration
entries.docstring:
The chiral scalar configuration: a complex value for each chiral label. This is
the sector's only field data. Declared as an `abbrev` so that unification sees
through it to `ChiralIndexingType → ℂ` and applies Mathlib's function-space calculus
lemmas directly.
entries.snippet: abbrev ChiralScalarConfiguration (ChiralIndexingType : Type*)

entries.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor
entries.docstring:
The four colours carried by a chiral-sector index: holomorphy (`chiral` versus
`anti`, a scalar versus its complex conjugate) crossed with variance (`up` versus
`down`, contravariant versus covariant). Carrying both axes here lets the single index
type `ι` label the scalars.
entries.snippet: inductive ChiralColor | chiralUp | chiralDown | antiUp | antiDown

entries.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.tau
entries.docstring:
The dual colour: flips variance and preserves holomorphy. Two indices may contract
exactly when their colours are `τ`-related, so `V^I` pairs only with `V_I` (same
holomorphy, opposite variance) and never with a conjugate index.
entries.snippet:
def tau : ChiralColor → ChiralColor
  | chiralUp => chiralDown
  | chiralDown => chiralUp
  | antiUp => antiDown
  | antiDown => antiUp

entries.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.bar
entries.docstring:
The conjugate colour: flips holomorphy (`chiral`↔`anti`) and preserves variance. Complex
conjugation sends an index to its conjugate carrier, so `bar` swaps `chiral*` with `anti*`.
Distinct from the variance dual `tau`; the two commute (`bar_tau`).
entries.snippet:
def bar : ChiralColor → ChiralColor
  | chiralUp => antiUp
  | antiUp => chiralUp
  | chiralDown => antiDown
  | antiDown => chiralDown

entries.name: SUSY.N1.chiralModule
entries.docstring:
The carrier module of each colour, distinct for all four: the holomorphic vectors `ι → ℂ` and
their dual `Module.Dual ℂ (ι → ℂ)` on the chiral side, and the conjugate module `ConjModule …` of
each (where `i` acts as `−i`) on the anti side. Variance is the vector/dual axis, holomorphy the
conjugate-module axis; both are genuine carrier data, not labels tracked separately.
entries.snippet:
abbrev chiralModule : ChiralColor → Type
  | .chiralUp   => ι → ℂ
  | .chiralDown => Module.Dual ℂ (ι → ℂ)
  | .antiUp     => ConjModule (ι → ℂ)
  | .antiDown   => ConjModule (Module.Dual ℂ (ι → ℂ))

entries.name: SUSY.N1.instAddCommGroupChiralModule
entries.snippet:
instance instAddCommGroupChiralModule : ∀ c, AddCommGroup (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)
  | .chiralUp | .chiralDown | .antiUp | .antiDown => inferInstance

entries.name: SUSY.N1.instModuleChiralModule
entries.snippet:
noncomputable instance instModuleChiralModule : ∀ c, Module ℂ (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)
  | .chiralUp | .chiralDown | .antiUp | .antiDown => inferInstance

entries.name: SUSY.N1.chiralRep
entries.docstring:
The representation on each colour, taken trivial over the trivial group `Unit`: the chiral
scalars carry no charge in this sector.
entries.snippet: def chiralRep : (c : ChiralColor) → Representation ℂ Unit (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)

entries.name: SUSY.N1.piBasis
entries.docstring:
The standard basis of the vector carrier `ι → ℂ` (the indicator functions); the basis of
`chiralUp` and the reference basis for the δ pairing.
entries.snippet: def piBasis : Basis ι ℂ (ι → ℂ)

entries.name: SUSY.N1.chiralBasis
entries.docstring:
The basis of each colour's carrier, all indexed by `ι`: `piBasis` on the holomorphic vectors,
its dual `piBasis.dualBasis` on the holomorphic covectors, and the `Basis.conj` of each on the
anti-holomorphic side (coordinates `star`-ed).
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def chiralBasis : (c : ChiralColor) → Basis ι ℂ (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)
  | .chiralUp   => piBasis
  | .chiralDown => piBasis.dualBasis
  | .antiUp     => Basis.conj piBasis
  | .antiDown   => Basis.conj piBasis.dualBasis

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaCap
entries.docstring:
The δ cap `∑_I b_I ⊗ b_I`: the rank-2 tensor in `M ⊗ M` with two upper indices, whose
components in the basis `b` are `δⁱʲ`. It is an element of `M ⊗ M` (the inverse-metric "cap"),
not a linear map, and serves as the `metric` field of the species (whose two slots share a
colour).
entries.snippet: def deltaCap (b : Basis ι ℂ M) : M ⊗[ℂ] M

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaBil₂
entries.docstring:
The δ pairing between two based modules sharing the index `ι`: the dot product of coordinate
vectors `(x, y) ↦ ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`. Built from Mathlib's `Basis.toDual b` (the canonical δ map
`M → Module.Dual M`, sending `b` to its dual basis) precomposed on the second slot with the basis
transport `b' ≃ b`.
entries.snippet: def deltaBil₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M →ₗ[ℂ] N →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaBil₂_apply
entries.docstring: `deltaBil₂ b b' x y = ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaBil₂_apply (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaBil₂ b b' x y = ∑ I, b.equivFun x I * b'.equivFun y I

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂
entries.docstring: The two-module δ contraction `M ⊗ N → ℂ`.
entries.snippet: def deltaContr₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M ⊗[ℂ] N →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_tmul
entries.docstring: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_tmul (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] y) = ∑ I, b.equivFun x I * b'.equivFun y I

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_tmul_basis
entries.docstring: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ b' J) = x_J`: pairing with the second basis reads off a coordinate.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_tmul_basis (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (J : ι) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b' J) = b.equivFun x J

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_basis_basis
entries.docstring: `deltaContr₂ b b' (b I ⊗ₜ b' J) = δ_{IJ}`: the two bases are δ-dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_basis_basis (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (I J : ι) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (b I ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b' J) = if I = J then 1 else 0

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_comm
entries.docstring: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = deltaContr₂ b' b (y ⊗ₜ x)`: swapping slots swaps the two bases.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_comm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] y) = deltaContr₂ b' b (y ⊗ₜ[ℂ] x)

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaCap₂
entries.docstring: The two-module δ cap `∑_I b_I ⊗ b'_I ∈ M ⊗ N`.
entries.snippet: def deltaCap₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M ⊗[ℂ] N

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaCap₂_comm
entries.docstring: `comm (deltaCap₂ b b') = deltaCap₂ b' b`: swapping the two factors swaps the two bases.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaCap₂_comm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) :
    TensorProduct.comm ℂ M N (deltaCap₂ b b') = deltaCap₂ b' b

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaUnit₂_symm
entries.docstring:
The `unit_symm` law (two-module, `toSpanSingleton` form): `deltaCap₂ b' b` is the swap of
`deltaCap₂ b b'`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaUnit₂_symm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) :
    LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b' b) 1 =
      LinearMap.lTensor N (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ M).toLinearMap
        (TensorProduct.comm ℂ M N (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b b') 1))

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_unit
entries.docstring:
The snake identity (two-module, `contr_unit` law): contracting `x ∈ M` into the `M`-leg of
`deltaCap₂ b' b ∈ N ⊗ M` returns `x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_unit (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) :
    (TensorProduct.lid ℂ M) ((deltaContr₂ b b').rTensor M
      ((TensorProduct.assoc ℂ M N M).symm
        (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b' b) 1))) = x

entries.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_metric
entries.docstring:
The `contr_metric` law (two-module): contracting the inner `M`/`N` legs of
`deltaCap b ⊗ deltaCap b'` yields `deltaCap₂ b' b`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deltaContr₂_metric (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) :
    (TensorProduct.comm ℂ M N ((TensorProduct.lid ℂ N).lTensor M
      (((deltaContr₂ b b').rTensor N).lTensor M
        (((TensorProduct.assoc ℂ M N N).symm.toLinearMap.lTensor M)
          ((TensorProduct.assoc ℂ M M (N ⊗[ℂ] N))
            (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap b) 1 ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
              LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap b') 1)))))) =
      LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b' b) 1

entries.name: SUSY.N1.chiralTensor
entries.docstring:
The chiral-index tensor species, bundled with its conjugation. Its four colours
`chiral`/`anti` × `up`/`down` carry the four distinct carriers of §C. `contr c` is the two-module δ
pairing of a colour against its variance dual `τ c` (`V c ⊗ V (τ c) → ℂ`); `unit c` is the δ cap
across those two carriers; `metric c` is the single-colour δ cap `∑_I b_I ⊗ b_I`. Each
`TensorSpecies` coherence law reduces, by case analysis on the colour, to the corresponding abstract
two-module δ lemma of §D. The conjugation flips holomorphy (`ChiralColor.bar`) while preserving
variance; every basis is indexed by `ι`, so `barIdx_eq` is `rfl`, and `conj_contrComm` is
`star δ = δ`. Instantiating `ConjTensorSpecies` this way gives the chiral sector both
the framework's generic tensor API and its conjugation API (`conjT` and its laws) on one object.
entries.snippet:
def chiralTensor : ConjTensorSpecies ℂ ChiralColor Unit (chiralModule (ι := ι)) (fun _ => ι)
    (chiralRep (ι := ι)) (chiralBasis (ι := ι)) where

entries.name: SUSY.N1.conjScalar
entries.docstring: Conjugation of a scalar tensor, normalized back to the scalar colour list `![]`.
entries.snippet:
def conjScalar (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![]) :
    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![]

entries.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector
entries.docstring:
Conjugation of a holomorphic covector, normalized to the anti-holomorphic covector colour
list `![antiDown]`.
entries.snippet:
def conjChiralCovector
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![antiDown]

entries.name: SUSY.N1.toField_conjScalar
entries.docstring:
For scalar tensors, `toField` of the normalized tensor conjugate is the complex conjugate of
`toField`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toField_conjScalar (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![]) :
    (conjScalar t).toField = star t.toField

entries.name: SUSY.N1.repr_conjChiralCovector
entries.docstring:
Component formula for the holomorphic covector conjugate: the `![I]` basis component of
`conjChiralCovector t` is the complex conjugate of the `![I]` component of `t`.
entries.snippet:
lemma repr_conjChiralCovector
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) (I : ι) :
    (basis (S := (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).toTensorSpecies) ![antiDown]).repr
        (conjChiralCovector t) ![I] =
      star ((basis (S := (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).toTensorSpecies) ![chiralDown]).repr t ![I])

entries.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector_add
entries.docstring: Conjugation of a holomorphic covector is additive.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma conjChiralCovector_add
    (t₁ t₂ : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    conjChiralCovector (t₁ + t₂) = conjChiralCovector t₁ + conjChiralCovector t₂

entries.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector_smul
entries.docstring:
Conjugation of a holomorphic covector is conjugate-linear: a scalar `r` pulls out as
`star r`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma conjChiralCovector_smul (r : ℂ)
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    conjChiralCovector (r • t) = star r • conjChiralCovector t

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsLowerBound
entries.docstring: `IsLowerBound T z c` is the property that `c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖T x - z • x‖` for all `x : T.domain`.
entries.snippet: def IsLowerBound (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) (c : ℝ) : Prop

entries.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_neg

lemma isLowerBound_neg {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z c) :
    IsLowerBound (-T) (-z) c

entries.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_of_right_le
entries.snippet:
lemma isLowerBound_of_right_le
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hle : c₁ ≤ c₂) (h : IsLowerBound T z c₂) :
    IsLowerBound T z c₁

entries.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_of_left_le
entries.snippet:
lemma isLowerBound_of_left_le
    {T₁ T₂ : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hle : T₁ ≤ T₂) {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T₂ z c) :
