entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain
entries.docstring:
The regular points for `T`.

  `z : ℂ` is a regular point for `T` iff there exists a constant `c > 0` such that
  `c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖(T - z • 1) x‖` for all `x ∈ T.domain`.
entries.snippet: def regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_neg
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma regularityDomain_neg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : (-T).regularityDomain = -T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_smul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma regularityDomain_smul (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    (w • T).regularityDomain = w • T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_antitone
entries.docstring: `T ≤ T'` implies `T'.regularityDomain ⊆ T.regularityDomain`.
entries.snippet: lemma regularityDomain_antitone : Antitone (regularityDomain (H := H))

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_regularityDomain_iff
entries.docstring:
`z` is a regular point for `T` iff `T - z • 1` has
  a continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_regularityDomain_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ T.regularityDomain ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

entries.name: LinearPMap.ball_subset_regularityDomain
entries.docstring: The regularity domain of `T` contains open balls with radii controlled by the lower bounds.
entries.snippet:
lemma ball_subset_regularityDomain
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z c) : ball z c ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_isOpen
entries.docstring: The regularity domain is an open set.
entries.snippet: lemma regularityDomain_isOpen (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : IsOpen T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_closure
entries.docstring: `T` and `T.closure` have the same regularity domain.
entries.snippet:
lemma regularityDomain_closure (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    T.closure.regularityDomain = T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.closure_range_sub_eq_range_closure_sub
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosable.closure_range_sub_eq_range_closure_sub [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    (T - z • 1).toFun.range.closure = (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.range

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.sub_range_isClosed
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.sub_range_isClosed [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    _root_.IsClosed ((T - z • 1).toFun.range : Set H)

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_closure_sub_range
entries.docstring: `(T.closure - z • 1).rangeᗮ = (T† - conj z • 1).ker`
entries.snippet:
lemma IsUnbounded.orthogonal_closure_sub_range [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsUnbounded) (z : ℂ) :
    (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ
      = (T† - conj z • 1).toFun.ker.map (T† - conj z • 1).domain.subtype

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_sub_ker
entries.docstring: `(T† - conj z • 1).kerᗮ = (T.closure - z • 1).range`
entries.snippet:
lemma IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_sub_ker [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsUnbounded) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    ((T† - conj z • 1).toFun.ker.map (T† - conj z • 1).domain.subtype)ᗮ
      = (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.range

entries.name: LinearPMap.deficiencySubspace
entries.docstring:
For a partial linear map `T` and any complex number `z`, the closed submodule which
  is orthogonal to the range of `T - z • 1`.

  `T.defectNumber z` is defined as the rank of this subspace.
entries.snippet: def deficiencySubspace (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) : ClosedSubmodule ℂ H

entries.name: LinearPMap.deficiencySubspace_coe
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma deficiencySubspace_coe (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) :
    T.deficiencySubspace z = (T - z • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ

entries.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber
entries.docstring: The rank of `T.deficiencySubspace z = (T - z • 1).rangeᗮ`.
entries.snippet: def defectNumber (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) : Cardinal

entries.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma defectNumber_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) :
    T.defectNumber z = Module.rank ℂ (T.deficiencySubspace z)

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.defectNumber_eq_zero_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.defectNumber_eq_zero_iff [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    T.defectNumber z = 0 ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤

entries.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber_closure
entries.docstring: `T` and `T.closure` have the same defect number at points in their regularity domain.
entries.snippet:
lemma defectNumber_closure [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    T.closure.defectNumber z = T.defectNumber z

entries.name: Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_rank_lt
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_rank_lt
    {E F : Submodule ℂ H} [E.HasOrthogonalProjection] (h_rank : Module.rank ℂ E < Module.rank ℂ F) :
    Eᗮ ⊓ F ≠ ⊥

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.exists_inner_eq_zero_of_defectNumber_lt
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.exists_inner_eq_zero_of_defectNumber_lt [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} (hz₁ : z₁ ∈ T.regularityDomain) (h : T.defectNumber z₁ < T.defectNumber z₂) :
    ∃ x : T.domain, x ≠ 0 ∧ ⟪T x - z₁ • x, T x - z₂ • x⟫_ℂ = 0

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.defectNumber_eq_of_mem_ball
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosable.defectNumber_eq_of_mem_ball [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z₁ c) (h_ball : z₂ ∈ ball z₁ c) :
    T.defectNumber z₁ = T.defectNumber z₂

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.defectNumber_const
entries.docstring: The defect number is constant on each connected component of the regularity domain.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosable.defectNumber_const [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} (hz : z₂ ∈ connectedComponentIn T.regularityDomain z₁) :
    T.defectNumber z₁ = T.defectNumber z₂

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange
entries.docstring: The set `{⟪x, T x⟫_ℂ | x ∈ T.domain ∧ ‖x‖ = 1} ⊆ ℂ`.
entries.snippet: def numericalRange (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_eq
entries.snippet: lemma numericalRange_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θ T = (fun x ↦ ⟪↑x, T x⟫_ℂ) '' {x | ‖x‖ = 1}

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_numericalRange
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_numericalRange {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : T.domain} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    (‖x‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ * ⟪↑x, T x⟫_ℂ ∈ Θ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_nonempty
entries.snippet: lemma numericalRange_nonempty {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.domain ≠ ⊥) : (Θ T).Nonempty

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_neg
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma numericalRange_neg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θ (-T) = -Θ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_smul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma numericalRange_smul (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (c : ℂ) : Θ (c • T) = c • Θ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_sub_const
entries.snippet: lemma numericalRange_sub_const (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (c : ℂ) : Θ (T - c • 1) = Θ T - {c}

entries.name: LinearPMap.compl_closure_numericalRange_subset_regularityDomain
entries.docstring: The regularity domain contains the exterior of the numerical range.
entries.snippet:
lemma compl_closure_numericalRange_subset_regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    (_root_.closure (Θ T))ᶜ ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.exists_phase_add_im_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
private lemma exists_phase_add_im_eq_zero (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) :
    ∃ θ : ℝ, (exp (I * θ) * z₁ + exp (-I * θ) * z₂).im = 0

entries.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_convex
entries.docstring: The Toeplitz-Hausdorff theorem.
entries.snippet: theorem numericalRange_convex (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Convex ℝ (Θ T)

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet
entries.docstring:
The resolvent set, `ρ`, of a partial linear map.

  A complex number `z` is in `ρ T` iff the linear map `T - z • 1` from `T.domain` to `H`
  is a bijection with continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse.
entries.snippet: def resolventSet (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma resolventSet_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    ρ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)}

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_resolventSet_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_resolventSet_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ ρ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_eq_empty
entries.docstring: If an operator is not closed then its resolvent set is empty.
entries.snippet: lemma resolventSet_eq_empty [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (h : ¬T.IsClosed) : ρ T = ∅

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_subset_regularityDomain
entries.snippet: lemma resolventSet_subset_regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : ρ T ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.resolventSet_eq
entries.docstring:
For a closed operator the continuity of the resolvent is redundant
  in the definition of the resolvent set.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.resolventSet_eq [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) :
    ρ T = {z : ℂ | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤}

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.resolventSet_eq'
entries.docstring:
For a closed operator the resolvent set consists of those regular points for which
  the defect number is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.resolventSet_eq' [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) :
    ρ T = T.regularityDomain ∩ T.defectNumber ⁻¹' {0}

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_isOpen
entries.docstring: The resolvent set is an open subset of ℂ.
entries.snippet: lemma resolventSet_isOpen [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : IsOpen (ρ T)

entries.name: LinearPMap.spectrum
entries.docstring:
The spectrum, `σ`, of a partial linear map.

  `σ T` is the complement of `ρ T`. A complex number `z` is in `σ T` iff the linear map `T - z • 1`
  from `T.domain` to `H` fails to be bijective or `(T - z • 1)⁻¹` is not continuous
  (equivalently, is not bounded).
entries.snippet: def spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_eq
entries.snippet: lemma spectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σ T = (ρ T)ᶜ

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_spectrum_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_spectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ σ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥ ∨ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∨ ¬Continuous (𝑅 T z)

entries.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_eq_univ
entries.docstring: If an operator is not closed then its spectrum is all of ℂ.
entries.snippet: lemma spectrum_eq_univ [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (h : ¬T.IsClosed) : σ T = univ

entries.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_isClosed
entries.docstring: The spectrum is a closed subset of ℂ.
entries.snippet: lemma spectrum_isClosed [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : _root_.IsClosed (σ T)

entries.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum
entries.docstring:
The point spectrum, `σᵖ`, of a partial linear map.

  A complex number `z` is in `σᵖ T` iff `T - z • 1` is not injective.
entries.snippet: def pointSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_eq
entries.snippet: lemma pointSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥}

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_pointSpectrum_iff
entries.snippet: lemma mem_pointSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} : z ∈ σᵖ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥

entries.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_subset_spectrum
entries.snippet: lemma pointSpectrum_subset_spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T ⊆ σ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum
entries.docstring:
The residual spectrum, `σʳ`, of a partial linear map.

  A complex number `z` is in `σʳ T` iff `T - z • 1` is injective but not surjective
  and `(T - z • 1)⁻¹` is continuous (equivalently, bounded).
entries.snippet: def residualSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma residualSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    σʳ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)}

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_residualSpectrum_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_residualSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ σʳ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

entries.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_subset_spectrum
entries.snippet: lemma residualSpectrum_subset_spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σʳ T ⊆ σ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_subset_regularityDomain
entries.snippet: lemma residualSpectrum_subset_regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σʳ T ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum
entries.docstring:
The continuous spectrum, `σᶜ`, of a partial linear map.

  A complex number `z` is in `σᶜ T` iff the range of `T - z • 1` is not closed.
entries.snippet: def continuousSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

entries.name: LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma continuousSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    σᶜ T = {z | ¬_root_.IsClosed ((T - z • 1).toFun.range : Set H)}

entries.name: LinearPMap.mem_continuousSpectrum_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_continuousSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ σᶜ T ↔ ¬_root_.IsClosed ((T - z • 1).toFun.range : Set H)

entries.name: LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum_subset_spectrum
entries.snippet: lemma continuousSpectrum_subset_spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᶜ T ⊆ σ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.spectrum_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma IsClosed.spectrum_eq [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) :
    σ T = σᵖ T ∪ σʳ T ∪ σᶜ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_inter_residualSpectrum
entries.snippet: lemma pointSpectrum_inter_residualSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T ∩ σʳ T = ∅

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolvent_sub
entries.snippet:
lemma resolvent_sub
    {T₁ T₂ : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T₂.domain ≤ T₁.domain) {z : ℂ} (hz₁ : z ∈ ρ T₁) (hz₂ : z ∈ ρ T₂) :
    𝑅 T₁ z - 𝑅 T₂ z = 𝑅 T₁ z * (T₂ - T₁) * 𝑅 T₂ z

entries.name: LinearPMap.resolvent_sub'
entries.snippet:
lemma resolvent_sub' {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (hz₁ : z₁ ∈ ρ T) (hz₂ : z₂ ∈ ρ T) :
    𝑅 T z₁ - 𝑅 T z₂ = (z₁ - z₂) • (𝑅 T z₁ * 𝑅 T z₂)

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.resolventSet_eq_regularityDomain
entries.snippet: lemma resolventSet_eq_regularityDomain : ρ T = T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.mem_resolventSet_of_range_eq_top
entries.docstring:
`(T - z • 1).range = ⊤` is a sufficient condition for `z ∈ ρ T`
  (and it is a necessary condition by definition of `ρ`).
entries.snippet: lemma mem_resolventSet_of_range_eq_top {z : ℂ} (h : (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤) : z ∈ ρ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.spectrum_real
entries.docstring: The spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is real.
entries.snippet: lemma spectrum_real : σ T ⊆ range ofReal

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.residualSpectrum_eq_empty
entries.docstring: The residual spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is empty.
entries.snippet: lemma residualSpectrum_eq_empty : σʳ T = ∅

entries.name: SpectralMeasure
entries.docstring:
A _spectral measure_ on a measurable space `α` is a σ-additive function `Set α → H →L[ℂ] H`
  such that each set is mapped to a star projection on `H`, the empty set and non-measurable sets
  are mapped to zero, and `univ` is mapped to the identity.
entries.snippet:
structure SpectralMeasure
    (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α]
    (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    extends VectorMeasure α (H →L[ℂ] H) where
  isStarProjection' : ∀ A, IsStarProjection (measureOf' A)
  univ' : measureOf' univ = 1

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.instCoeVectorMeasure
entries.snippet: instance instCoeVectorMeasure : Coe (SpectralMeasure α H) (VectorMeasure α (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.instCoeFun
entries.snippet: instance instCoeFun : CoeFun (SpectralMeasure α H) fun _ ↦ Set α → H →L[ℂ] H

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.isStarProjection
entries.snippet: lemma isStarProjection (A : Set α) : IsStarProjection (μS A)

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.univ
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma univ : μS univ = 1

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.comp_self
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma comp_self (A : Set α) : μS A ∘L μS A = μS A

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.comp_of_disjoint
entries.snippet:
lemma comp_of_disjoint
    {A B : Set α} (h : Disjoint A B) (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    μS A ∘L μS B = 0

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.comp_eq_of_inter
entries.snippet:
lemma comp_eq_of_inter {A B : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    μS A ∘L μS B = μS (A ∩ B)

entries.name: SpectralMeasure.commute
entries.snippet: lemma commute (A B : Set α) : Commute (μS A) (μS B)

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.realNumericalRange
entries.docstring: The projection of the numerical range onto the real axis.
entries.snippet: def realNumericalRange (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℝ

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.realNumericalRange_eq
entries.snippet: lemma realNumericalRange_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θᵣₑ T = re '' Θ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.realNumericalRange_neg
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma realNumericalRange_neg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θᵣₑ (-T) = -Θᵣₑ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.im_eq_zero_of_mem_numericalRange
entries.docstring: The numerical range of a symmetric operator is contained in the real axis.
entries.snippet: lemma im_eq_zero_of_mem_numericalRange {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Θ T) : z.im = 0

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.numericalRange_subset
entries.docstring: The numerical range of a symmetric operator is contained in the real axis.
entries.snippet: lemma numericalRange_subset : Θ T ⊆ range ofReal

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.numericalRange_eq
entries.docstring: The numerical range of a symmetric operator is equal to its projection onto the real axis.
entries.snippet: lemma numericalRange_eq : Θ T = ofReal '' Θᵣₑ T

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.closure_numericalRange_subset
entries.snippet: lemma closure_numericalRange_subset : _root_.closure (Θ T) ⊆ range ofReal

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.mem_regularityDomain_of_im_ne_zero
entries.docstring:
The regularity domain of a symmetric operator contains all complex numbers with non-zero
  imaginary part.
entries.snippet: lemma mem_regularityDomain_of_im_ne_zero {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) : z ∈ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.compl_ofReal_subset_regularityDomain
entries.docstring:
The regularity domain of a symmetric operator contains all complex numbers with non-zero
  imaginary part.
entries.snippet: lemma compl_ofReal_subset_regularityDomain : (range ofReal)ᶜ ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.Iio_subset_regularityDomain
entries.docstring: If `m` is a lower bound on the numerical range then the regularity domain contains `(-∞,m)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma Iio_subset_regularityDomain {m : ℝ} (h : m ∈ lowerBounds (Θᵣₑ T)) :
    ofReal '' Iio m ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.Ioi_subset_regularityDomain
entries.docstring: If `m` is an upper bound on the numerical range then the regularity domain contains `(m,∞)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma Ioi_subset_regularityDomain {m : ℝ} (h : m ∈ upperBounds (Θᵣₑ T)) :
    ofReal '' Ioi m ⊆ T.regularityDomain

entries.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.regularityDomain_isConnected_iff
entries.docstring: The regularity domain of a symmetric operator is connected iff it contains a real number.
entries.snippet:
lemma regularityDomain_isConnected_iff :

entries.name: LinearMap.continuous_iff_bounded
entries.docstring:
`f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F` is continuous iff there exists `M > 0` s.t. `‖f x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖` for all `x : E`.

  This is a (convenient) immediate consequence of
  `IsBoundedLinearMap.isLinearMap_and_continuous_iff_isBoundedLinearMap`.

lemma _root_.LinearMap.continuous_iff_bounded {𝕜 E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]

    {f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F} : Continuous f ↔ ∃ M, 0 < M ∧ ∀ x : E, ‖f x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖

entries.name: Fermion.leftHandedToDual

entries.name: Fermion.leftDualContraction
entries.docstring:
The linear map from leftHandedWeyl ⊗ DualLeftHandedWeyl to ℂ given by
    summing over components of leftHandedWeyl and DualLeftHandedWeyl in the
    standard basis (i.e. the dot product).
    Physically, the contraction of a left-handed Weyl fermion with a dual-left-handed Weyl fermion.
    In index notation this is ψ^a φ_a.
entries.snippet:
def leftDualContraction : (leftHandedRep.tprod dualLeftHandedRep).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) ℂ) where

entries.name: Fermion.leftDualContraction_apply_metric
entries.snippet:
lemma leftDualContraction_apply_metric :
    (TensorProduct.comm ℂ _ _ <|
      (TensorProduct.lid ℂ _).lTensor _ <|
      (leftDualContraction.toLinearMap.rTensor _).lTensor _ <|
      (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap.lTensor _<|
      TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ (_ ⊗[ℂ] _) <|
      (leftMetric 1) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (dualLeftMetric 1)) = dualLeftLeftUnit (1 : ℂ)

    (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap.lTensor _<|

    (dualLeftMetric 1) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (leftMetric 1)) = leftDualLeftUnit (1 : ℂ)

entries.name: Fermion.rightDualContraction_apply_metric
entries.snippet:
lemma rightDualContraction_apply_metric :
    (TensorProduct.comm ℂ _ _ <|
    (TensorProduct.lid ℂ _).lTensor _ <|
    (rightDualContraction.toLinearMap.rTensor _).lTensor _ <|
    (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap.lTensor _<|
    TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ (_ ⊗[ℂ] _) <|
    (rightMetric 1) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (dualRightMetric 1)) = dualRightRightUnit (1 : ℂ)

entries.name: Fermion.dualRightContraction_apply_metric
entries.snippet:
lemma dualRightContraction_apply_metric :
    (TensorProduct.comm ℂ _ _ <|
      (TensorProduct.lid ℂ _).lTensor _ <|
      (dualRightContraction.toLinearMap.rTensor _).lTensor _ <|
      (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap.lTensor _<|
      TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ (_ ⊗[ℂ] _) <|
      (dualRightMetric 1) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (rightMetric 1)) = rightDualRightUnit (1 : ℂ)

entries.name: Fermion.dualLeftdualLeftToMatrix_ρ
entries.docstring:
The group action of `SL(2,ℂ)` on `dualLeftHanded ⊗ dualLeftHanded` is equivalent to
  `(M.1⁻¹)ᵀ * leftLeftToMatrix v * (M.1⁻¹)`.

    (M.1⁻¹)ᵀ * dualLeftdualLeftToMatrix v * (M.1⁻¹)

  the invariance under the `SL(2,ℂ)` action.

entries.name: Fermion.dualRightRightUnitVal

The dual-right-right unit `δ_{dot a}^{dot a}` as an element of

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies
entries.docstring:
A tensor species bundled with a conjugation. Beyond the `TensorSpecies` it `extends`, it carries
the conjugate-colour involution `bar`, the index-set identification `barIdx_eq`, and the
contraction-coherence `conj_contrComm`. Also carries `bar_involution` and `bar_tau` (that `bar` is
involutive and commutes with the variance dual).
entries.snippet:
structure ConjTensorSpecies (k : Type) [CommRing k] [StarRing k] (C : Type) (G : Type) [Group G]
    (V : C → Type) [∀ c, AddCommGroup (V c)] [∀ c, Module k (V c)]
    (basisIdx : C → Type) [∀ c, Fintype (basisIdx c)] [∀ c, DecidableEq (basisIdx c)]
    (rep : (c : C) → Representation k G (V c)) (b : (c : C) → Basis (basisIdx c) k (V c))
    extends TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b where
  bar : C → C
  bar_involution : Function.Involutive bar
  bar_tau : ∀ c, bar (toTensorSpecies.τ c) = toTensorSpecies.τ (bar c)
  barIdx_eq : ∀ c, basisIdx (bar c) = basisIdx c
  conj_contrComm : ∀ (d : C) (x₁ : basisIdx d) (x₂ : basisIdx (toTensorSpecies.τ d)),
      star (toTensorSpecies.contr d (b d x₁ ⊗ₜ[k] b (toTensorSpecies.τ d) x₂))
        = toTensorSpecies.contr (bar d) (b (bar d) ((Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq d)).symm x₁) ⊗ₜ[k]
            b (toTensorSpecies.τ (bar d)) (basisIdxCongr (bar_tau d)
              ((Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq (toTensorSpecies.τ d))).symm x₂)))

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.componentReindex
entries.docstring: Reindex component labels of `bar ∘ c` back to `c`, slotwise via the cast `barIdx_eq`.
entries.snippet:
def componentReindex {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) :
    ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (S.bar ∘ c) ≃ ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) c

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT
entries.docstring:
Conjugation of a tensor: conjugate the components and reindex the basis to the conjugate
colours. `conj`-semilinear by construction (see `conjT_smul`).
entries.snippet: def conjT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c) : S.Tensor (S.bar ∘ c)

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_eq_permT_iff
entries.docstring:
Componentwise criterion for `conjT t = permT σ h t'`. The conjugate of `t` equals the
recolouring `permT σ h t'` exactly when, at every component, the `star`-conjugated reindexed
component of `t` matches the corresponding component of `permT σ h t'`. This packages the
`componentMap_conjT` expansion and the `repr`/`componentMap` bridge that the reality and Hermiticity
proofs downstream would otherwise repeat by hand; the caller is left only with the species-specific
permutation bookkeeping on the right-hand side.
entries.snippet:
lemma conjT_eq_permT_iff {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c' : Fin m → C}
    {σ : Fin n → Fin m} (h : IsReindexing c' (S.bar ∘ c) σ)
    (t : S.Tensor c) (t' : S.Tensor c') :
    S.conjT t = permT σ h t' ↔
      ∀ φ : ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (S.bar ∘ c),
        star (componentMap c t (S.componentReindex c φ))
          = (Tensor.basis (S.bar ∘ c)).repr (permT σ h t') φ

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.barIdx_involutive_symm
entries.docstring:
Undoing the two cast reindexings (at `bar c` then at `c`) on a label of the doubly-conjugated
colour returns the `bar_involution` cast. Free from `barIdx_eq` by `cast_cast` + proof
irrelevance, with no coherence field needed.

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isReindexing_bar_bar
entries.docstring:
The identity permutation satisfies `IsReindexing` from `c` to `bar ∘ bar ∘ c`, as `bar` is an
involution.
entries.snippet:
lemma isReindexing_bar_bar {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) :
    IsReindexing c (S.bar ∘ S.bar ∘ c) (id : Fin n → Fin n)

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_conjT
entries.docstring:
Conjugation is an involution: conjugating twice returns the original tensor, up to the
`bar_involution` recolouring (the identity permutation `permT`).
entries.snippet:
lemma conjT_conjT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT (S.conjT t)
      = permT id (S.isReindexing_bar_bar c) t

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.contrCond_bar
entries.docstring: Slots with dual colour in `c` have dual colour in `bar ∘ c`, as `bar` commutes with `τ`.

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_contrT
entries.docstring:
Conjugation commutes with contraction: conjugating a contracted tensor equals contracting the
conjugate on the `bar`-images of the same two slots.
entries.snippet:
lemma conjT_contrT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (h : i ≠ j ∧ S.τ (c i) = c j) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT (contrT n i j h t)
      = contrT n i j (S.contrCond_bar h) (S.conjT t)

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv
entries.docstring:
The conjugate-linear slot isomorphism `V c ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] V (bar c)`: conjugate the
coordinates in the species basis and relabel to the conjugate colour via `barIdx_eq`.
entries.snippet: def conjEquiv {c : C} : V c ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] V (S.bar c)

entries.name: ConjTensorSpecies.IsHermitian
entries.docstring:
A pairing `g : V c ⊗ V (bar c) → k` is Hermitian when conjugating and swapping its two slots
via `conjEquiv` returns its `star`: `g (x ⊗ y) = star (g (conjEquiv.symm y ⊗ conjEquiv x))`.
entries.snippet: def IsHermitian {c : C} (g : V c ⊗[k] V (S.bar c) →ₗ[k] k) : Prop

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_eq_pure
entries.snippet:
lemma fromPairT_eq_pure {c1 c2 : C} (x : V c1) (y : V c2) :
    fromPairT (S := S) (x ⊗ₜ[k] y) = Pure.toTensor (fun | 0 => x | 1 => y)

entries.name: Fin.apply_succSuccAbove_symm
entries.snippet:
@[simp, nolint simpVarHead]
lemma apply_succSuccAbove_symm {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (k : Fin n) : c (succSuccAbove i j k) = c (succSuccAbove j i k)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.evalT_basis_single
entries.docstring:
Evaluating the single-index basis tensor `basis ![c] (single.symm b)` at the index `x`
  yields the field element `1` if `b = x` (transported across `![c] 0 = c`) and `0` otherwise:
  evaluation of a one-index basis tensor is the Kronecker delta.
entries.snippet:
lemma evalT_basis_single {c : C} (b : basisIdx c) (x : basisIdx (![c] 0)) :
    (evalT 0 x (basis (S := S) ![c] (ComponentIdx.single.symm b))).toField =
    if basisIdxCongr (by simp) b =  x then 1 else 0

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.eq_sum_evalT_of_single_tensor_basis
entries.docstring:
Basis expansion of a one-index tensor: every `t : Tensor S ![c]` is the sum over basis
  indices `i` of its evaluation coefficient `toField (evalT 0 i t)` times the corresponding
  basis tensor.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_sum_evalT_of_single_tensor_basis {c : C} (t : Tensor S ![c]) :
    t = ∑ i, toField (evalT 0 i t) • basis ![c] (ComponentIdx.single.symm
      (basisIdxCongr (by simp) i))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.eq_sum_evalT
entries.docstring:
Reconstruction of a tensor from the evaluations of its last index: every `t : Tensor S c`
  is the sum over basis indices `i` of the evaluation `evalT (Fin.last n) i t` tensored with
  the basis covector `basis ![c (Fin.last n)] (single.symm i)`, with the appended index
  permuted back into the last slot.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_sum_evalT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (t : Tensor S c) :
    t = ∑ i, permT id (IsReindexing.append_succ_last c) (prodT (evalT (Fin.last n) i t)
      (basis ![c (Fin.last n)] (ComponentIdx.single.symm i)))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.eq_sum_evalT_zero
entries.docstring:
Reconstruction of a tensor from the evaluations of its first index: every `t : Tensor S c`
  is the sum over basis indices `i` of the basis covector `basis ![c 0] (single.symm i)` tensored
  with the evaluation `evalT 0 i t`, with the prepended index permuted back into the first slot.
  This is the first-index analogue of `eq_sum_evalT`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_sum_evalT_zero {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (t : Tensor S c) :
    t = ∑ i, permT _ (IsReindexing.append_of_first c)
    (prodT (basis ![c 0] (ComponentIdx.single.symm i)) (evalT 0 i t))

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita tensor `εᵘᵛᵖᵟ` as a real Lorentz tensor in `d = 3`, with `ε⁰¹²³ = 1`.

The component on a multi-index `f` is the generalized Kronecker delta of `f` against the
identity, i.e. the sign of `f` when `f` is a permutation and `0` otherwise.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def leviCivita : ℝT[3, .up, .up, .up, .up]

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_eq_ofInt
entries.docstring: The `TensorInt.toTensor` form of the Levi-Civita tensor.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_eq_ofInt : ε4 =
    TensorInt.toTensor (S := realLorentzTensor 3)
    (c := ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up]) fun f =>
    generalizedKroneckerDelta (fun i => finSumFinEquiv (f i)) (id : Fin 4 → Fin 4)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_basis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
The components of the Levi-Civita tensor in the standard basis are the generalized
Kronecker delta of the multi-index against the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_basis_repr_apply
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3) ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b
      = (generalizedKroneckerDelta (fun i => finSumFinEquiv (b i)) (id : Fin 4 → Fin 4) : ℝ)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_basis_repr_eq_zero_of_eq
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita tensor vanishes on any multi-index with a repeated value: if two distinct
index positions `i ≠ j` carry the same basis index, the component is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_basis_repr_eq_zero_of_eq
    {b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3) ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up]}
    {i j : Fin 4} (hij : i ≠ j) (h : b i = b j) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b = 0

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_antisymm
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita tensor is antisymmetric in its first two indices
`{ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - ε4 | ν μ ρ σ}ᵀ`.
entries.snippet: lemma leviCivita_antisymm : {ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - (ε4 | ν μ ρ σ)}ᵀ

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_antisymm_mid
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita tensor is antisymmetric in its middle two indices
`{ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - ε4 | μ ρ ν σ}ᵀ`.
entries.snippet: lemma leviCivita_antisymm_mid : {ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - (ε4 | μ ρ ν σ)}ᵀ

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_antisymm_last
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita tensor is antisymmetric in its last two indices
`{ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - ε4 | μ ν σ ρ}ᵀ`.
entries.snippet: lemma leviCivita_antisymm_last : {ε4 | μ ν ρ σ = - (ε4 | μ ν σ ρ)}ᵀ

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.prodP_update_left
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma Pure.prodP_update_left {n1 n2} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c1 : Fin n2 → C}
    (p1 : Pure S c) (p2 : Pure S c1) (i : Fin n1) (x : V (c i)) :
    Pure.prodP (Pure.update p1 i x) p2
    = Pure.update (Pure.prodP p1 p2) (Fin.castAdd n2 i)
      (LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by simp) x)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.prodP_update_right
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma Pure.prodP_update_right {n1 n2} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c1 : Fin n2 → C}
    (p1 : Pure S c) (p2 : Pure S c1) (i : Fin n2) (x : V (c1 i)) :
    Pure.prodP p1 (Pure.update p2 i x)
    = Pure.update (Pure.prodP p1 p2) (Fin.natAdd n1 i)
      (LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by simp) x)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.prodP_update_add_toTensor_left
entries.snippet:
lemma Pure.prodP_update_add_toTensor_left {n1 n2} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c1 : Fin n2 → C}
    (p1 : Pure S c) (p2 : Pure S c1) (i : Fin n2) (x y : V (c1 i)) :
    (Pure.prodP p1 (Pure.update p2 i (x + y))).toTensor
    = (Pure.prodP p1 (Pure.update p2 i x)).toTensor
    + (Pure.prodP p1 (Pure.update p2 i y)).toTensor

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.prodT_basis'
entries.snippet:
lemma prodT_basis' {n1 n2} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c1 : Fin n2 → C}
    (b : ComponentIdx c) (b1 : ComponentIdx (S := S) c1) :
    (basis c b).prodT (basis c1 b1) =
    basis (Fin.append c c1) (ComponentIdx.prod.symm (b, b1))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing
entries.docstring:
Given two lists of indices `c : Fin n → C` and `c1 : Fin m → C` a map
  `σ : Fin m → Fin n` satisfies the condition `IsReindexing c c1 σ` if it is:
- A bijection
- Forms a commutative triangle with `c` and `c1`.
entries.snippet:
def IsReindexing {n m : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (c1 : Fin m → C)
    (σ : Fin m → Fin n) : Prop

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.injective
entries.snippet:
lemma injective {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    {σ : Fin m → Fin n} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) : Function.Injective σ

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.surjective
entries.snippet:
lemma surjective {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.auto
TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.on_id
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma on_id {n : ℕ} {c c1 : Fin n → C} :

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.on_id_symm
entries.snippet:
lemma on_id_symm {n : ℕ} {c c1 : Fin n → C} (h : IsReindexing c1 c id) :
    IsReindexing c c1 (id : Fin n → Fin n)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_congr_left
entries.snippet:
lemma append_congr_left {n n' n2 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c' : Fin n' → C}
    {σ : Fin n' → Fin n} (c2 : Fin n2 → C) (h : IsReindexing c c' σ) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c c2) (Fin.append c' c2)
      (Fin.append (Fin.castAdd n2 ∘ σ) (Fin.natAdd n))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_congr_right
entries.snippet:
lemma append_congr_right {n n' n2 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c' : Fin n' → C}
    {σ : Fin n' → Fin n} (c2 : Fin n2 → C) (h : IsReindexing c c' σ) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c2 c) (Fin.append c2 c')
      (Fin.append (Fin.castAdd n) (Fin.natAdd n2 ∘ σ))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_zero_right
entries.snippet:
lemma append_zero_right {n} {c : Fin n → C}
    {c1 : Fin 0 → C} : IsReindexing c (Fin.append c c1) id

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_swap
entries.snippet:
lemma append_swap {n n2 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c2 : Fin n2 → C} :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c c2) (Fin.append c2 c)
      (Fin.append (Fin.natAdd n) (Fin.castAdd n2))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_assoc_right
entries.snippet:
lemma append_assoc_right   {n1 n2 n3 : ℕ} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c2 : Fin n2 → C} {c3 : Fin n3 → C} :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c (Fin.append c2 c3)) (Fin.append (Fin.append c c2) c3)
      (Fin.cast (by grind))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_assoc_left
entries.snippet:
lemma append_assoc_left {n1 n2 n3 : ℕ} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c2 : Fin n2 → C} {c3 : Fin n3 → C} :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append (Fin.append c c2) c3) (Fin.append c (Fin.append c2 c3))
      (Fin.cast (by grind))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_succAbove_natAdd
entries.snippet:
lemma append_succAbove_natAdd {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin (n1 + 1) → C}
    (i : Fin (n1 + 1)) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c c1 ∘ (Fin.natAdd n i).succAbove)
      (Fin.append c (c1 ∘ i.succAbove)) id

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_succAbove_castAdd
entries.snippet:
lemma append_succAbove_castAdd {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} {c1 : Fin (n1 + 1) → C}
    (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c c1 ∘ (Fin.castAdd (n1 + 1) i).succAbove)
      (Fin.append (c ∘ i.succAbove) c1) (Fin.cast (by grind))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_succSuccAbove_natAdd
entries.docstring:
Removing two entries from the right component of `Fin.append c1 c` commutes with the
  append: removing the `i`-th and `j`-th entries of `c` and then appending `c1` matches
  removing the corresponding entries of `Fin.append c1 c`, via the identity permutation.
  This is used for the commutation of taking a *product* of tensors
  with *contraction* of indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma append_succSuccAbove_natAdd {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C}
    {c1 : Fin n1 → C} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append c1 c ∘ (Fin.natAdd n1 i).succSuccAbove (Fin.natAdd n1 j))
      (Fin.append c1 (c ∘ i.succSuccAbove j)) id

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succAbove_of_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
Given a reindexing of `c` by `c1` via `σ` for which the index `i` is sent to `0`,
  removing the `i`-th entry of `c1` and the first entry of `c` yields a reindexing of
  `c ∘ Fin.succ` by `c1 ∘ i.succAbove` via the map sending `j` to the predecessor of
  `σ (i.succAbove j)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma succAbove_of_eq_zero {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} {c1 : Fin (n1 + 1) → C}
    {σ : Fin (n1 + 1) → Fin (n + 1)} (i : Fin (n1 + 1))
    (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (hi : σ i = 0) :
    IsReindexing (c ∘ Fin.succ) (c1 ∘ i.succAbove)
      (fun j => (σ (i.succAbove j)).pred (by simp [← hi, h.injective.eq_iff]))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succAbove_of_neq_zero
entries.docstring:
Given a reindexing of `c` by `c1` via `σ` for which the index `i` is not sent to `0`,
  removing the `i`-th entry of `c1` and the `(σ i)`-th entry of `c` yields a reindexing of
  `c ∘ (σ i).succAbove` by `c1 ∘ i.succAbove` via the map
  `(σ i).pred.predAbove ∘ σ ∘ i.succAbove`.
entries.snippet:
lemma succAbove_of_neq_zero {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} {c1 : Fin (n1 + 1) → C}
    {σ : Fin (n1 + 1) → Fin (n + 1)} (i : Fin (n1 + 1))
    (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (hi : σ i ≠ 0) :
    IsReindexing (c ∘ (σ i).succAbove) (c1 ∘ i.succAbove)
      ((Fin.pred (σ i) hi).predAbove  ∘ σ ∘ i.succAbove)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succAbove
entries.docstring:
Given a reindexing of `c` by `c1` via `σ`, removing the `i`-th entry of `c1` and the
  `(σ i)`-th entry of `c` yields a reindexing of `c ∘ (σ i).succAbove` by `c1 ∘ i.succAbove`.
  This unifies `succAbove_of_eq_zero` and `succAbove_of_neq_zero` via a case split on
  whether `σ i = 0`. This is used for the commutation of *permutation*
  of indices with *evaluation* of indices.

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succSuccAbove
entries.docstring:
Given a reindexing of `c` by `c1` via `σ` and two distinct indices `i ≠ j`, removing the
  `i`-th and `j`-th entries of `c1` and the `(σ i)`-th and `(σ j)`-th entries of `c` yields a
  reindexing of `c ∘ (σ i).succSuccAbove (σ j)` by `c1 ∘ i.succSuccAbove j`.
  This is used for the commutation of *permutation* of indices with
  *contraction* of indices.

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succSuccAbove_comm
entries.docstring:
Removing two pairs of entries from `c` in either order gives the same colour list:
  removing the `i1`-th and `j1`-th entries and then the (shifted) `i2`-th and `j2`-th entries
  matches removing the `i2`-th and `j2`-th entries first and then the (shifted) `i1`-th and
  `j1`-th entries, via the identity permutation.
  This is used for the commutation of two *contractions*.
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_comm {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1) → C}
    (i1 j1 : Fin (n + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1)) (i2 j2 : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (hij1 : i1 ≠ j1) (hij2 : i2 ≠ j2) :
    let i2'

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succAbove_succSuccAbove_comm
entries.docstring:
Removing one entry and then a pair of entries from `c` in either order gives the same
  colour list: removing the `k`-th entry and then the (shifted) `i`-th and `j`-th entries
  matches removing the `i`-th and `j`-th entries first and then the (shifted) `k`-th entry,
  via the identity permutation.
  This is used for the commutation of a *contraction* with an *evaluation*.

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.succAbove_succAbove_comm
entries.docstring:
Removing two single entries from `c` in either order gives the same colour list:
  removing the `k1`-th entry and then the (shifted) `k2`-th entry matches removing the
  `k2`-th entry first and then the (shifted) `k1`-th entry, via the identity permutation.
  This is used for the commutation of two *evaluations* of indices.

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_succ_last
entries.docstring:
Splitting a list of colours `c : Fin (n + 1) → C` into its first `n` entries and its
  last entry recovers `c`: the identity permutation matches
  `Fin.append (c ∘ (Fin.last n).succAbove) ![c (Fin.last n)]` with `c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma append_succ_last {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → C) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append (c ∘ (Fin.last n).succAbove) ![c (Fin.last n)]) c id

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.append_of_first
entries.docstring:
Splitting a list of colours `c : Fin (n + 1) → C` into its first entry and its remaining
  `n` entries recovers `c`: the canonical reindexing `Fin (1 + n) ≃ Fin (n + 1)` matches
  `Fin.append ![c 0] (c ∘ Fin.succAbove 0)` with `c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma append_of_first {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → C) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append ![c 0] (c ∘ Fin.succAbove 0)) c (Fin.cast (by grind))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.fin_cast_isReindexing
entries.docstring:
Casting the domain along an equality `n1 = n` of lengths is a reindexing of `c` by
  `c ∘ Fin.cast h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma fin_cast_isReindexing (n n1 : ℕ) {c : Fin n → C} (h : n1 = n) :
    IsReindexing c (c ∘ Fin.cast h) (Fin.cast h)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensorial.prod_eq_sum_eval
entries.docstring:
Double basis expansion of an element of a tensor product `M ⊗[k] M₂` of two `Tensorial`
  one-index spaces. Given bases `b`, `b2` of `M`, `M₂` coming from the single-index tensor bases,
  every `x : M ⊗[k] M₂` is the double sum over `i, j` of the iterated evaluation coefficient
  `toField (evalT 0 j (evalT 0 i (toTensor x)))` times `b i ⊗ₜ b2 j`.

entries.name: TensorSpecies.basisIdxCongr_heq_arg
entries.docstring:
`basisIdxCongr` only depends on its endpoints up to `HEq` of the arguments: equal target
colours and heterogeneously equal labels give equal casts.
entries.snippet:
lemma basisIdxCongr_heq_arg {c1 c2 d : C} (h1 : c1 = d) (h2 : c2 = d)
    {x : basisIdx c1} {y : basisIdx c2} (hxy : HEq x y) :
    basisIdxCongr h1 x = basisIdxCongr h2 y

entries.name: GalileanGroup
entries.docstring:
A Galilean transformation in `d` spatial dimensions. The fields are, in order, the spatial
orthogonal part, boost velocity, spatial translation, and time translation.
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
structure GalileanGroup (d : ℕ := 3) where
  rotation : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ
  velocity : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  spaceTranslation : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  timeTranslation : Time

entries.name: GalileanGroup.orthogonal_smul_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma orthogonal_smul_smul (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    R • (c • v) = c • (R • v)

entries.name: GalileanGroup.one_timeTranslation

lemma one_timeTranslation : (1 : GalileanGroup d).timeTranslation = 0

entries.name: GalileanGroup.«instance@2d436bb6»
entries.docstring: The product whose action is composition: `(g * h) • tx = g • h • tx`.
entries.snippet: instance : Mul (GalileanGroup d) where

entries.name: GalileanGroup.mul_rotation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mul_rotation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).rotation = g.rotation * h.rotation

entries.name: GalileanGroup.mul_velocity
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mul_velocity (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).velocity = g.rotation • h.velocity + g.velocity

entries.name: GalileanGroup.mul_spaceTranslation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mul_spaceTranslation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).spaceTranslation =
      g.spaceTranslation + g.rotation • h.spaceTranslation + h.timeTranslation.val • g.velocity

entries.name: GalileanGroup.mul_timeTranslation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mul_timeTranslation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).timeTranslation = g.timeTranslation + h.timeTranslation

entries.name: GalileanGroup.«instance@3107b840»
entries.docstring: The inverse Galilean transformation.
entries.snippet: instance : Inv (GalileanGroup d) where

entries.name: GalileanGroup.inv_rotation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inv_rotation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.rotation = g.rotation⁻¹

entries.name: GalileanGroup.inv_velocity
entries.docstring: The inverse boost velocity formula.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inv_velocity (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.velocity = -(g.rotation⁻¹ • g.velocity)

entries.name: GalileanGroup.inv_spaceTranslation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inv_spaceTranslation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.spaceTranslation =
      -(g.rotation⁻¹ • g.spaceTranslation) +
        g.timeTranslation.val • (g.rotation⁻¹ • g.velocity)

entries.name: GalileanGroup.inv_timeTranslation
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inv_timeTranslation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.timeTranslation = -g.timeTranslation

entries.name: GalileanGroup.smul_fst
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smul_fst (g : GalileanGroup d) (tx : Time × Space d) :
    (g • tx).1 = tx.1 + g.timeTranslation

entries.name: GalileanGroup.smul_snd
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smul_snd (g : GalileanGroup d) (tx : Time × Space d) :
    (g • tx).2 = g.actSpace tx.1 tx.2

entries.name: GalileanGroup.smul_mk
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smul_mk (g : GalileanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) :
    g • ((t, x) : Time × Space d) = (t + g.timeTranslation, g.actSpace t x)

entries.name: GalileanGroup.actSpace_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma actSpace_apply (g : GalileanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    g.actSpace t x i =
      (g.rotation • (x -ᵥ (0 : Space d))) i + t.val * g.velocity i + g.spaceTranslation i

entries.name: Space.deriv_sub

    (f1 f2 : Space d → M) (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :

entries.name: Space.distCurl_coord_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma distCurl_coord_apply {i : Fin 3}
    (f : Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) (η : 𝓢(Space, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⨯ f) η i = - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+2)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+1)
    + f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+1)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+2)

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.«instance@6372eb27»
entries.docstring:
The action of the Euclidean group on the affine space of points `Space d`: `g = ⟨t, Q⟩` rotates
`p` about the coordinate origin by the orthogonal part `Q` and then translates by `t`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : MulAction (EuclideanGroup d) (Space d) where

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.dist_smul
entries.docstring: The Euclidean group acts on `Space d` **by isometries**: every rigid motion preserves distance.
entries.snippet:
lemma dist_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p q : Space d) :
    dist (g • p) (g • q) = dist p q

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_smul_vsub_origin
entries.docstring:
A rotation acts on the displacement from the origin by its orthogonal part, for every `p`:
`(r • p) -ᵥ origin = Q • (p -ᵥ origin)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma rotation_smul_vsub_origin (r : RotationGroup d) (p : Space d) :
    (r • p) -ᵥ (0 : Space d) = (r : EuclideanGroup d).linear • (p -ᵥ (0 : Space d))

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_dist_smul
entries.docstring: The rotation group acts on `Space d` **by isometries** (inherited from `dist_smul`).
entries.snippet:
lemma rotation_dist_smul (r : RotationGroup d) (p q : Space d) :
    dist (r • p) (r • q) = dist p q

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.chartEuclidean_smul
entries.docstring:
Under the standard chart, the Euclidean action on `Space d` is the
transport of `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv` acting on `EuclideanSpace`:
`chart (g • p) = (toAffineIsometryMulEquiv g) (chart p)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma chartEuclidean_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p : Space d) :
    Space.chartEuclidean d (g • p) = toAffineIsometryMulEquiv g (Space.chartEuclidean d p)

entries.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout

elements of the form T(p) * r * T(-p) with T(·) : translationVector.incl n (Multiplicative.ofAdd ·)
and r : RotationGroup where r is viewed as a rotation about the origin. Note T(-p) = T(p)⁻¹.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def RotationsAbout : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n) where

entries.name: Space.integrable_spherical_of_integrable
entries.snippet:
lemma integrable_spherical_of_integrable {d : ℕ} {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {f : Space d → F}
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    Integrable
      (fun x : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1) × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) =>
        f (x.2.1 • x.1.1))
      (volume (α := Space d).toSphere.prod
        (Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1)))

entries.name: Space.integral_volume_eq_spherical_iterated
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_volume_eq_spherical_iterated {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : Space d, f x =
      ∫ n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1),
        ∫ r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), f (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1))
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

entries.name: Space.integral_volume_eq_spherical_integral
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_volume_eq_spherical_integral {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : Space d, f x =
      ∫ n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1),
        ∫ r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), (r.1 ^ (d - 1)) • f (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

entries.name: Space.radial_jacobian_zpow_mul_self
entries.snippet:
lemma radial_jacobian_zpow_mul_self
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] {q : ℤ} (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    r ^ (d - 1) * (r ^ q * r) = r ^ p

entries.name: Space.radial_jacobian_zpow
entries.snippet:
private lemma radial_jacobian_zpow
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] {q : ℤ} (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    (hp_pos : 0 < p) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    r ^ (d - 1) * r ^ q = r ^ (p - 1)

entries.name: Space.radial_norm_power_spherical_integral_eq_space_integral
entries.snippet:
lemma radial_norm_power_spherical_integral_eq_space_integral
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] {q : ℤ} (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    (hp_pos : 0 < p) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    ∫ x : Space d, η x * ‖x‖ ^ q =
      ∫ (n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1)),
        ∫ (r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)),
          r.1 ^ (p - 1) * η (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

entries.name: Space.norm_smul_sphere
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_smul_sphere {d : ℕ} (n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1))
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    ‖(r • (n : Space d))‖ = r

entries.name: Space.integrable_real_pow_mul_schwartz
entries.snippet:
private lemma integrable_real_pow_mul_schwartz
    (ψ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℝ)) (k : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k * ψ x) volume

entries.name: Space.radial_power_deriv_integral_by_parts
entries.snippet:
private lemma radial_power_deriv_integral_by_parts
    {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ))
    (n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1))
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    - ∫ (r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)),
        r.1 ^ p * (_root_.deriv (fun a => η (a • n.1)) r.1)
        ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)
      =
      (p : ℝ) * ∫ (r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)),
        r.1 ^ (p - 1) * η (r.1 • n.1)
        ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)

entries.name: Space.distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_apply_eq_radial_deriv
entries.snippet:
private lemma distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_apply_eq_radial_deriv
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] (q : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q + (d : ℤ))
    (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⬝ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ q • basis.repr x)
      (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self q (by omega)))) η =
      - ∫ n, (∫ (r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)),
        r.1 ^ p * (_root_.deriv (fun a => η (a • n.1)) r.1)
        ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume))
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

entries.name: Space.distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_eq_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_eq_smul
    {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (q : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q + (d : ℤ)) :
    ∇ᵈ ⬝ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ q • basis.repr x)
      (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self q (by omega))) =
      (((q + d : ℤ) : ℝ) •
        distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ q)
          (IsDistBounded.pow q (by omega)))

entries.name: Space.distLaplacian_distOfFunction_norm_zpow
entries.snippet:
lemma distLaplacian_distOfFunction_norm_zpow {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (m : ℤ)
    (hdiv : 0 < m - 2 + (d : ℤ)) :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ m)
      (IsDistBounded.pow m (by omega))) =
      (((m : ℝ) * (((m - 2 + d : ℤ) : ℝ))) •
        distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ (m - 2))
          (IsDistBounded.pow (m - 2) (by omega)))

entries.name: Space.distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_norm_zpow
entries.docstring:
The distributional Laplacian of `‖x‖ ^ (2 - d)` is `(2 - d) * d * volume (Metric.ball 0 1)`
times the Dirac delta at the origin. For `d ≥ 3` this `‖x‖ ^ (2 - d)` is the (singular)
fundamental solution of the Laplacian, and for `d = 1` it is `‖x‖`. When `d = 2` the exponent
vanishes, so the identity collapses to the trivial `Δᵈ 1 = 0`; the genuine two-dimensional
fundamental solution is the logarithm, proved in `distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm`.
The statement also holds vacuously for `d = 0`, where the space is trivial.
entries.snippet:
lemma distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_norm_zpow {d : ℕ} :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ (- ((d : ℤ) - 2)))
      (IsDistBounded.pow _ (by omega))) =
      ((- ((d : ℝ) - 2)) * d *
        (volume (α := Space d)).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) • diracDelta ℝ 0

entries.name: Space.distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm
entries.docstring:
In dimension two the fundamental solution of the Laplacian is the logarithm: the
distributional Laplacian of `Real.log ‖x‖` is `2 * volume (Metric.ball 0 1)` times the Dirac
delta at the origin.
entries.snippet:
lemma distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space 2 => Real.log ‖x‖) IsDistBounded.log_norm) =
      (2 * (volume (α := Space 2)).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) • diracDelta ℝ 0

entries.docstring: The scalar factor in the odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff (m : ℕ) : ℝ

entries.name: Space.oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff_factor_ne_zero

entries.docstring: The scalar factor in the odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm is nonzero.
entries.snippet:

    oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff m ≠ 0

entries.name: Space.distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_boundary
entries.snippet:
private lemma distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_boundary (m : ℕ) :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space (2 * m + 1) =>
      ‖x‖ ^ ((1 : ℤ) - 2 * (m : ℤ)))
      (IsDistBounded.pow _ (by omega))) =
      (((1 : ℤ) - 2 * (m : ℤ) : ℝ) * (2 * m + 1 : ℝ) *
        (volume (α := Space (2 * m + 1))).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) •
          diracDelta ℝ 0

entries.name: Space.iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_until_boundary
entries.snippet:
private lemma iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_until_boundary
    (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) :
    ((distLaplacian (d := 2 * m + 1))^[k])
      (distOfFunction (fun x : Space (2 * m + 1) => ‖x‖ ^ (1 : ℤ))
        (IsDistBounded.pow 1 (by omega))) =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.range k,
          ((((1 : ℤ) - 2 * (j : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℝ) *
            ((((1 : ℤ) - 2 * (j : ℤ) - 2 + (2 * m + 1 : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℝ)))) •
        distOfFunction (fun x : Space (2 * m + 1) => ‖x‖ ^ ((1 : ℤ) - 2 * (k : ℤ)))
          (IsDistBounded.pow _ (by omega))

entries.name: Space.iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_eq_smul_diracDelta
entries.docstring:
In dimension `2 * m + 1`, the `(m + 1)`-fold distributional Laplacian of the
distribution induced by the norm is a nonzero multiple of the Dirac delta at the origin.
entries.snippet:
lemma iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_eq_smul_diracDelta (m : ℕ) :
    ((distLaplacian (d := 2 * m + 1))^[m + 1])
      (distOfFunction (fun x : Space (2 * m + 1) => ‖x‖ ^ (1 : ℤ))
        (IsDistBounded.pow 1 (by omega))) =
      oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff m • diracDelta ℝ 0

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction
entries.docstring:
The Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps over `TimeAndSpace d`, as a continuous
representation `ContRepresentation ℝ (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)`.

`ContRepresentation R G V` unfolds to the monoid homomorphism `G →* V →L[R] V` into the
*continuous*-linear maps: the builder `SchwartzMap.compCLMOfAntilipschitz` already yields a
continuous-linear map for free, and the `→L` codomain lets the action compose under `∘L`. The
plain mathlib `Representation` (`G →* V →ₗ[ℝ] V`) is recovered via
`ContRepresentation.toRepresentation`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def schwartzEuclideanAction {d : ℕ} :
    ContRepresentation ℝ (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F) where

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_apply
entries.docstring: Pointwise formula for the monoid-homomorphism form of the Schwartz-map pullback action.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_apply {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F))
    (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (schwartzEuclideanAction g η) tx = η (g⁻¹ • tx)

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.instMulActionSchwartzMap
entries.docstring: The Euclidean group acts on Schwartz maps over `TimeAndSpace d` by pullback.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable instance instMulActionSchwartzMap {d : ℕ} :
    MulAction (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F) where

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.smul_schwartzMap_apply
entries.docstring: Pointwise formula for the `MulAction` instance on Schwartz maps.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smul_schwartzMap_apply {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F))
    (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (g • η) tx = η (g⁻¹ • tx)

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_mul_apply
entries.docstring: Applying `g` and then `h` to a Schwartz map is the pullback action of `h * g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_mul_apply {d : ℕ} (g h : EuclideanGroup d)
    (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)) :
    schwartzEuclideanAction h (schwartzEuclideanAction g η) =
      schwartzEuclideanAction (h * g) η

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_injective
entries.docstring: Each Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps is injective.
entries.snippet:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_injective {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Function.Injective (schwartzEuclideanAction (F := F) g)

entries.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_surjective
entries.docstring: Each Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps is surjective.
entries.snippet:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_surjective {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Function.Surjective (schwartzEuclideanAction (F := F) g)

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference
entries.docstring:
Locality package for the action density under compactly supported variations: for every
variation parameter `s`, the change in the action density is a continuous compactly supported
function. Combined with finiteness of the base action, this implies finiteness of the varied
action.

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.hasFiniteActionVariation_of_hasFiniteAction_of_compactlySupportedDifference
entries.docstring:
If the base action is finite and every varied action density differs from the base density by
a continuous compactly supported function, then the whole varied family has finite action.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasFiniteActionVariation_of_hasFiniteAction_of_compactlySupportedDifference
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (hbase : HasFiniteAction L f)
    (hdiff : HasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference L f η) :
    HasFiniteActionVariation L f η

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsCritical
entries.docstring:
A field is critical for a local action if every admissible compactly supported variation has
vanishing first derivative at `s = 0`, under the explicit finite-action hypothesis for the varied
family.

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeTerm
entries.docstring: The summand `(-1)^|I| D_I (∂L/∂u^a_I)` in the local Euler-Lagrange formula.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def eulerLagrangeTerm (L : Lagrangian d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeTerm_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma eulerLagrangeTerm_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    eulerLagrangeTerm L I a f x =
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ I.1.order * iteratedTotalDerivative k I.1 (L.coordDeriv I a) f x

lemma eulerLagrangeComponent_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    eulerLagrangeComponent L a f x = ∑ I : DerivativeIndex d k, eulerLagrangeTerm L I a f x

lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :

entries.snippet:
noncomputable def firstVariationValue (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.firstVariationDensityTerm_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma firstVariationDensityTerm_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) (I : DerivativeIndex d k)
    (a : Fin m) (x : Space d) :
    firstVariationDensityTerm L f η I a x =
      L.coordDeriv I a (jetAt k f x) * ∂^[I.1] (fun y => (η y) a) x

    firstVariationDensity L f η x =
      ∑ I : DerivativeIndex d k, ∑ a : Fin m, firstVariationDensityTerm L f η I a x

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionVariation_hasDerivAt_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le
entries.docstring:
A direct bridge from Mathlib's dominated differentiation-under-the-integral theorem to the
local action variation. This isolates the measure-theoretic input needed to prove
`HasActionVariationDerivativeUnderIntegral`.
entries.snippet:
lemma actionVariation_hasDerivAt_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    {F' : ℝ → Space d → ℝ} {bound : Space d → ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hmeas :
      ∀ᶠ s in nhds (0 : ℝ),
        AEStronglyMeasurable (actionDensity L (variedField f η s)) volume)
    (hfinite0 : Integrable (actionDensity L (variedField f η 0)))
    (hF'_meas : AEStronglyMeasurable (F' 0) volume)
    (hbound :
      ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ s ∈ Metric.ball (0 : ℝ) ε, ‖F' s x‖ ≤ bound x)
    (hbound_int : Integrable bound volume)
    (hderiv :
      ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ s ∈ Metric.ball (0 : ℝ) ε,
        HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => actionDensity L (variedField f η r) x) (F' s x) s) :
    HasDerivAt (actionVariation L f η) (∫ x, F' 0 x) 0

private lemma firstVariationDensityTerm_norm_le_of_coeff_bound
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (ψ : DerivativeIndex d k → Fin m → Space d → ℝ)
    (hψ : ∀ I : DerivativeIndex d k, ∀ a : Fin m, ∀ x : Space d,
      ψ I a x = ∂^[I.1] (fun y => (η y) a) x)
    (C : DerivativeIndex d k → Fin m → ℝ)
    (K : DerivativeIndex d k → Fin m → Set (Space d))
    (hKzero : ∀ I : DerivativeIndex d k, ∀ a : Fin m, ∀ x, x ∉ K I a → ψ I a x = 0)
    (hC : ∀ I : DerivativeIndex d k, ∀ a : Fin m,
      ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ K I a,
        ‖L.coordDeriv I a (jetAt k (variedField f η p.1) p.2)‖ ≤ C I a)
    {x : Space d} {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Metric.ball (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    ‖firstVariationDensityTerm L (variedField f η s) η I a x‖ ≤ C I a * ‖ψ I a x‖

    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m)
    (hcont : Continuous (fun x : Space d =>
      L.coordDeriv I a (jetAt k f x))) :
    Integrable (firstVariationDensityTerm L f η I a)

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.continuous_jetBaseCoordinates_variedField
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_jetBaseCoordinates_variedField
    (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) :
    Continuous
      (fun p : ℝ × Space d => (p.2, jetCoordinatesAt k (variedField f η p.1) p.2))

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetCoordinates
entries.docstring:
Coordinate data `u^a_I` for `k`-th order jet points.

For each derivative index `I`, these are the scalar components of the corresponding
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)` fiber coordinate. We keep this componentwise form because the
local Euler-Lagrange formulas are indexed by both `I` and `a`.
entries.snippet: abbrev JetCoordinates (d m k : ℕ)

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint
entries.docstring:
The coordinate-level points of the locally trivialized `k`-jet bundle for fields
`Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.
entries.snippet:
structure JetPoint (d m k : ℕ) where
  base : Space d
  fiber : JetCoordinates d m k

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.coord
entries.docstring: The coordinate `u^a_I` of a jet point.
entries.snippet: def coord (J : JetPoint d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.value
entries.docstring: The zero-th order value encoded by a jet point.
entries.snippet: def value (J : JetPoint d m k) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.value_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma value_apply (J : JetPoint d m k) (a : Fin m) :
    J.value a = J.coord 0 a

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ext
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
lemma ext (J K : JetPoint d m k) (hbase : J.base = K.base)
    (hcoord : ∀ I a, J.coord I a = K.coord I a) :
    J = K

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates
entries.docstring: Build a jet point from a base point and its jet coordinates.
entries.snippet: def ofBaseCoordinates (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) : JetPoint d m k where

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.toBaseCoordinates
entries.docstring: The base point and jet coordinates of a jet point.
entries.snippet: def toBaseCoordinates (J : JetPoint d m k) : Space d × JetCoordinates d m k

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_base
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_base (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_fiber
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_fiber (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_coord
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_coord (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (ofBaseCoordinates x u).coord I a = u I a

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_base_fiber
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_base_fiber (J : JetPoint d m k) :

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.toBaseCoordinates_ofBaseCoordinates
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toBaseCoordinates_ofBaseCoordinates (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :

entries.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt
entries.docstring: The jet-coordinate function determined by a field `g`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def jetCoordinatesAt (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
